items.title: From Clever Hans to Hypotheses: Interpreting EEG Foundational Transformers with LRP
items.summary: arXiv:2605.11885v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Emerging foundation models (FMs) in electroencephalography (EEG) promise a path to scale deep learning in diagnostics and brain-computer interfaces despite data scarcity, yet their opaque nature remains a barrier to wider adoption. We investigate attention-aware Layer-wise relevance propagation (LRP) as a post-hoc attribution method for EEG-FMs, extending LRP's use on convolutional neural network (CNN)-based EEG models to the Transformer architectures that current FMs are based on. We find that LRP can both verify EEG-FM decisions and surface novel, biologically plausible hypotheses from them. In motor imagery, it unmasks 'Clever…

items.title: EEG-FM-Audit: A Systematic Evaluation and Analysis Pipeline for EEG Foundation Models
items.summary: arXiv:2605.26910v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: EEG foundation models (EEG-FMs) show potential for learning generalized representations from heterogeneous EEG signals. However, existing studies exhibit three critical limitations: opaque model tuning, unverified contributions of complex learning paradigms to EEG-FMs, and a limited understanding of the neurophysiological features that FMs rely on to make decisions. To address these challenges, we propose EEG-FM-Audit, a systematic evaluation and diagnostic pipeline comprising three modules: (1) a fairness-calibrated benchmarking protocol ensuring fair comparisons through model-tailored hyperparameter optimization for EEG-FMs and…

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Literacy of College Students and Their Ethical Utilization
items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) offers opportunities for learning in higher education while raising concerns about academic integrity, privacy, bias, and misinformation. This study examined AI literacy and ethical AI utilization among second-year Bachelor of Secondary Education major in Science students at City College of Calapan and investigated their relationship as a basis for proposing an institutional framework. A quantitative descriptive-correlational design was employed, involving 43 respondents purposively selected from a population of 48 students. Data were analyzed using weighted means and Pearson’s correlation coefficient. Findings revealed high AI literacy in technical knowledge…

items.title: Enhancing Reservoir Characterization of a South Caspian Field Through Foundation Model-Based Log Prediction and Integrated Petrophysical Analysis
items.summary: This paper presents an integrated petrophysical characterization workflow for the Field in the South Caspian Basin. The study combines advanced measurements, including NMR and core laboratory data, with machine-learning-based log reconstruction to improve reservoir evaluation in wells with limited logging data and enhance inputs for geological modeling. A multimineral ELAN model was built for a calibration well using conventional logs, NMR measurements, and core analysis data. Porosity was determined using an integrated approach tailored to reservoir conditions and data quality. Permeability was estimated using a multiple linear regression model calibrated to core permeability data with…

items.title: Dual-Memory Enhancement for Fully Analog Memristive Time Delay Reservoirs
Human Mycelium: What Happens Between People
items.summary: The concept of human mycelium I am exploring here today builds upon the patterns described in my earlier essay, Mesh + Mycelium. That essay was about one person's own system or network. This one is about what happens between people. Here I use the word for the way people connect and interact. For the week I was there, Morelia was an ambient society for me, where connection is part of getting through a day. I experience my society at home as an arranging society. AI is changing how I connect and interact. What will working with AI do to both kinds of societies, the ambient and the arranging? In each new situation, we can all rebalance our connections.

items.title: WorldLatent: A Unified 4D Latent Space for World Perception and Generation
items.summary: Generative Pre-Training (GPT) represents a profound milestone in natural language processing, serving as the foundation for most of today's state-of-the-art large language models. By casting diverse understanding and generation problems into a shared token representation, GPT enables a single architecture and unified optimization loop to master heterogeneous tasks across massive corpora, giving rise to powerful foundation models for natural language. In contrast, 4D spatiotemporal vision lacks a common representational protocol: perception (such as depth and camera estimation) and generation are either handled by separate one-way pipelines or bolted together from unaligned single-modality…

items.title: JAISP: A Joint Rubin-Euclid Foundation Model for Cross-Instrument Source Detection and Astrometry
items.summary: Joint pixel-level processing of Rubin and Euclid imaging promises deeper source detection and the cross-survey consistency that precision cosmology requires. We introduce JAISP (Joint AI Survey Processing), a foundation model that learns a single representation of ten-band imaging: Rubin ugrizy and Euclid VIS, Y, J, and H, from the first public releases over $\approx 0.2$ deg$^2$ of the ECDFS deep field. Trained without labels by predicting each band from the other nine, its frozen encoder drives small task-specific networks for source detection and astrometry. The detection network recovers nearly all VIS-selected Euclid Q1 catalog sources on held-out sky, and source injection shows that…

items.title: EEG Decoding in Context: A Framework for Tuning-Free EEG Foundation Models
items.summary: Electroencephalography (EEG) decoding is a central route toward brain-computer interfaces for communication, rehabilitation, cognitive assessment, and neurological monitoring. Recent EEG foundation models have substantially advanced reusable signal representations, but their downstream use still typically requires a task-specific decoder, gradient-based adaptation, and validation-driven model selection. We investigate a complementary foundation-model paradigm based on in-context learning: labeled EEG recordings define the decoding task as context, and new recordings are predicted without updating model parameters. We first pair raw EEG features with a pretrained general-purpose in-context…

items.title: FATCAT: Fault Injection Attacks Targeting Chip-level Alignment
items.summary: Model alignment is the primary safety and security mechanism for enforcing refusal of malicious prompts in modern foundation models; yet, existing adversarial evaluations implicitly assume underlying hardware integrity. In this paper, we present FATCAT, the first physical fault-injection attacks capable of eliminating refusal in modern large language and vision-language models. Specifically, we present a non-invasive electromagnetic (EM) fault injection attack targeting GPU-accelerated Systems-on-Chip with physical access, requiring neither software execution privileges nor model-layer access. By leveraging an autonomous Radio Frequency (RF) side-channel trigger to synchronize EM faults to…

items.title: RUIBench: What Makes a Good Robot-Use Interface?
items.summary: Foundation models can reason about complex physical tasks, yet translating this intelligence into reliable robot execution remains challenging. We argue that a critical, often overlooked factor is the robot-use interface (RUI), which determines how agents express and execute physical actions. To systematically study its impact, we introduce RUIBench, comprising 30 manipulation tasks across five suites spanning world knowledge, in-context learning, discovery, dynamic interaction, and contact-rich manipulation. We further develop RUIKit, a unified framework that crosses six action abstractions with two interaction forms, yielding 13 interfaces under shared perception and control. In…

items.title: MAASAI: A Tool-Augmented Multi-Agent System for Astronomical Data Analysis
items.summary: Modern astronomical workflows require the coordinated use of specialised software, scientific archives, heterogeneous data, and domain-specific knowledge. Advances in large language models and multimodal foundation models enable natural-language interaction with scientific data and tools. Realising this potential requires integrating these models with established scientific capabilities. We present MAASAI (Multi-agent Astronomy Assistant for Scientific Analysis and Inference), a modular multi-agent system combining foundation-model reasoning, retrieval-augmented knowledge, and specialised astronomical tools within a graph-based execution framework. MAASAI coordinates request preparation,…

items.title: RoFE: Rotated Frozen Embeddings for Low-Data Multimodal Tabular Learning
items.summary: Multimodal tabular learning combines tabular data with images and text, often in settings where labeled data are scarce. Tabular foundation models such as prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) offer a promising solution via in-context learning without task-specific training. However, modern image and text encoders produce embeddings with hundreds or thousands of dimensions, far exceeding the number of features encountered during PFN pretraining. Existing approaches bridge this gap using principal component analysis (PCA) to compress frozen embeddings. Surprisingly, we find that this PCA interface can underperform simple linear classifiers when labeled examples are scarce, even though PFNs are…

items.title: Degree three unramified cohomology of homogeneous spaces with finite stabilisers
items.summary: We provide an explicit formula for the third unramified cohomology group of homogeneous spaces of $\mathrm{SL}_n$ with finite stabilisers and a rational point, valid over an arbitrary field of characteristic prime to the order of the stabilisers. As a concrete application, we compute this group explicitly for every generalised quaternion group over an arbitrary field of characteristic 0, and settle Noether's problem over the rational numbers in the negative for those of order at least 16, thereby generalising a classical result of Serre. Over an algebraically closed field, our formula recovers and sharpens a theorem of Peyre; we further show that universal triviality of unramified…

items.title: Closure of averaged Einstein equations by DESI data
items.summary: We benchmark the hypothesis that the redshift dependence of postulated dark energy in the standard model, measured by the DESI collaboration, is a natural outcome of dark energy-free models of structure formation in general relativity. We recall fundamental results and the properties of averaged dust cosmologies that suggest to replace the dark energy equation of state through the nonperturbative impact of the inhomogeneous geometry. The relevant mechanism can be phrased in terms of an effective mean field description of inhomogeneities using the fluid analogy of a scalar field (the `morphon'). Without violating energy conditions this effective field exhibits a cross-over to phantom…

items.title: Déjà VAE: When Do Autoencoder Traces Reveal Generated Images?
items.summary: A latent diffusion model's output has already passed through its autoencoder, so a second round trip changes it very little. This "déjà vu" underlies reconstruction-based detectors of generated images; we analyse when it reveals a generated image and when it does not. Read by a frozen vision foundation model without training, the trace is strongest in intermediate layers, and, unlike pixel-level reconstruction error, it treats blur as a sign of a real image. It belongs to the generator's exact decoder: on Synthbuster, the exact decoders of Stable Diffusion 1.3, 1.4, 2 and XL are the strongest of eight autoencoders and catch 94-100% of their generators' images at a 5% false-alarm rate…

items.title: Demographic Encoding is Not Exposure: Fairness and Privacy in Chest X-ray Foundation Models
items.summary: Medical foundation models encode patient demographics and can reveal whether a patient was in the training set, and these properties are often treated as one problem. We tested whether they are aligned by measuring demographic encoding, diagnostic fairness gaps and membership-inference vulnerability on the same models. We trained 200 linear or multilayer-perceptron (MLP) heads on frozen BiomedCLIP, DINOv2 and RAD-DINO embeddings, with three seeds, and audited them on CheXpert and NIH ChestX-ray14. Demographic encoding explained almost no variance in patient vulnerability, and all 72 CheXpert associations were statistically equivalent to zero. Erasing linearly decodable demographics left…

items.title: Lorentz symmetry in self-supervised representation learning
items.summary: Self-supervised learning (SSL) and explicit physical inductive biases have driven major advances in jet tagging, yet they are typically pursued along separate tracks. In this work, we unify both paradigms by integrating the Lorentz-equivariant Geometric Algebra Transformer slim (L-GATr-slim) architecture with the LeJEPA framework for representation learning. Pre-training on 100 million jets from the JetClass dataset, we optimize towards a latent space, which is invariant across physics-motivated jet augmentations. We demonstrate that enforcing Lorentz symmetry in the latent space is critical for representation quality and that this can be achieved either architecturally or learned via…

items.title: RoboUniverse-10K: Toward the Scaling Era of Agentic Robotics via Real-to-Sim Environments
items.summary: Agentic Robotics, in which foundation models act as coding agents to control robots through executable programs, has emerged as a compelling paradigm for embodied intelligence. Yet unlike software engineering, where massive executable environments power post-training, robotics remains constrained by small, manual benchmarks and in-distribution evaluation. To bridge this gap, we introduce RoboUniverse-10K, 10,807 interactive, resettable, and verifiable physics environments built from real-world videos via an automated Real2Sim and quality assurance pipeline. Each runs in an isolated, Harbor-compatible harness that hides privileged states and grading logic to mirror real-world sensing. From…

items.title: Beyond Self-Consistency: Recursive Self-Improvement at Test Time
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) that continue improving after deployment (e.g., recursive self-improvement) offer a promising path toward general intelligence. Current test-time methods pursue this goal on unlabeled questions, primarily relying on self-consistency: they generate independent solutions and use majority voting to select an answer or construct training targets. This leaves earlier reasoning unused at inference and can reinforce an incorrect majority during training. Humans instead build on earlier attempts to preserve useful reasoning, correct mistakes and improve their problem-solving strategies. Following this principle, we propose Test-Time Recursive Self-Improvement (TT-RSI),…

items.title: Foresight Forcing: Learning Spatial Foresight for Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: Robotic manipulation policies can improve action prediction by anticipating how objects move and how their spatial relationships change. World Action Models (WAMs) learn to predict future visual observations, but their training objectives typically leave the underlying 3D geometric transitions implicit. To alleviate this problem, we introduce Foresight Forcing ($\mathcal{F}^{2}$), a WAM that learns a spatial transition representation from changes in a pretrained 3D feature space. During training, a frozen 3D foundation model extracts patch-wise feature differences from aligned current and future observations that provide dense supervision for geometry-aware feature transitions. We distill…

items.title: Tabular Foundation Models Are Surprisingly Effective In-Context Robot Learners
items.summary: Can foundation models pretrained for generic numerical prediction serve as in-context robot learners? We investigate this question through tabular foundation models (TFMs), which are pretrained to infer input-output relationships from labeled examples in context. We introduce TabAct, which casts visual imitation as numerical prediction: frozen visual features and robot proprioception form the inputs, future action chunks form the targets, and each demonstration time step provides one labeled example that conditions a frozen TFM for closed-loop control. The predictor receives no robot-specific training or target-task fine-tuning. With one target-task demonstration available to each method,…

items.title: Analytic $k$-essence Inflation
items.summary: In this work we develop a fully analytic $k$-essence inflation solution which is compatible with the observational constraints on inflation, without the need for the slow-roll assumption being imposed dynamically in the field equations. The analytic solution is obtained for a kinetic scalar sector of the form $K(X)= \frac{X^n}{X_s^{n-1}}$ and for the scalar field satisfying a tracking condition $\dotφ^2=γH^{-m}$. For this class of theories, the sound speed of the primordial curvature perturbations is constant, so no gradient instabilities occur in the theory. The Hubble rate, the scale factor and the scalar field can be analytically expressed as functions of the cosmic time, and the…

items.title: Noise-Immune Attractors in Stochastically Driven Non-Hermitian Systems
items.summary: Temporal stochastic fluctuations generically destroy quantum coherence and accelerate defect generation in driven quantum systems. Here, we demonstrate that non-Hermitian dynamics can fundamentally reverse this trend by stabilizing noise-resilient late-time states. By developing an exact noise master equation for non-Hermitian systems subject to Gaussian fluctuations, we uncover a projective noise-invariance mechanism governed by T-symmetry-broken Liouvillian attractors. This mechanism produces robust defect-density plateaus and yields an exact geometric classification into noise-independent, fully polarized, and continuously tunable regimes. We substantiate these results in an…

items.title: On the Fourier Analysis of the Einstein-Klein-Gordon System: Limiting Behaviour of the Fourier Coefficients
items.summary: We revisit the problem of computing the Fourier coefficients associated with the spherically symmetric massless-scalar field system in $(1+3)$ dimensions initiated in [10]. We rigorously derive computationally efficient formulas for these coefficients and then use them to establish their asymptotic behavior as the mode numbers tend to infinity, including the explicit determination of the leading-order coefficients. Our approach builds on the method developed in [12] and relies on two powerful algorithms for hypergeometric summation, due to Zeilberger and Gosper. These algorithms enable us to systematically derive first-order linear recurrence relations and obtain closed-form discrete…

items.title: All-in-one Spintronic Sensory Neurons for Magnetic Edge Intelligence
items.summary: Magnetic fields enable non-contact sensing through nonmagnetic materials, offering opportunities for magnetic edge intelligence in autonomous recognition, navigation, and control. However, directly converting magnetic stimuli into neural spikes for local neuromorphic processing remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate an all-in-one spintronic sensory neuron (SSN) based on spin-transfer-torque magnetic tunnel junctions (STT-MTJs) fabricated using a 40-nm magnetoresistive random-access memory (MRAM) process. By exploiting magnetic-field-modulated stochastic switching, the SSN enables probability-based sensing with an electrically tunable sensitive field window, allowing adaptive operation…

items.title: Exact analytic solutions for the $n=1$ chameleon field in planar systems with an arbitrary number of uniform layers
items.summary: Scalar fields have long been investigated as a potential dark energy candidate. Of these models, screened scalar fields like the chameleon have received interest due to their ability to avoid observational constraints. However, the non-linear nature of these models has led to there being only a small number of exact analytic solutions within the literature. In this work, we present exact analytic solutions for the $n=1$ chameleon model in a planar system consisting of $N$ discrete regions of uniform density. We compare these to the relevant approximate solutions within the literature. We also use our solutions to forecast constraints from CANNEX, a recent experiment devised to measure…

items.title: How Many Parameters Does Forecasting Need? A Survey and Code-Level Audit of Lightweight Long-Term Time Series Forecasting
items.summary: Long-term time series forecasting supports decisions in energy, transportation, weather and finance, where forecasts are produced continuously and often on constrained hardware. Recent work has moved in two directions. One scales Transformers and pre-trained foundation models to millions or hundreds of millions of parameters. The other shows that models with only hundreds to tens of thousands of parameters remain competitive on the standard benchmarks. Existing surveys organize forecasting models by backbone and treat efficiency as a side topic, so the reasons these small models work, and the way their sizes are reported, remain unexamined. This survey focuses on lightweight long-term…

items.title: Coherence transfer under bounded channel capacity
items.summary: We investigate quantum coherence transfer between two parties whose local reference bases are misaligned, under a constraint on the capacity of the quantum communication channel. Within the resource theory of coherence, we formulate the task as maximizing the coherence received by Bob when Alice is restricted to Maximally Incoherent Operations (MIO) in her local basis. We first analyze two single-shot protocols, based on direct and locally entangled transmission, and derive their phase-optimized coherence yields. We further investigate their performance when Bob's reference basis is unknown, averaging over uniformly distributed basis configurations. In the asymptotic regime, we exploit the…

items.title: DriveDreamer-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of Driving Perception and Agentic Data Generation
items.summary: Controllable generation can expand training data for driving perception, but visual realism alone does not ensure learning gains. Effective generation must adapt both what data to generate and how to construct them as the perception model evolves. In this paper, we present DriveDreamer-RSI, a framework for recursive self-improvement of driving perception and agentic data generation through feedback between perception learning and data construction. Its outer loop implements Gap-Guided Target Adaptation, generating labeled videos from current perception gaps and updating targets after training. Its inner loop uses a vision-language agent to iteratively edit scenes through observation and…

items.title: Quantifying superposition via coherence by stochastic orthogonalization
items.summary: Here we present an approach to quantifying superposition of nonorthogonal reference states through quantum coherence. No change of basis achieves this: every orthonormal basis makes some superposition-free states appear coherent. We show that orthogonalization succeeds instead as a measurement mapping every reference state onto a multiple of a basis vector in each outcome; such measurements are exactly the free operations that convert superposition into coherence. The largest average coherence they extract from a state, which we call its degree of superposition, turns every coherence measure into a superposition measure with the same operational meaning. items.title: Learning Multimodal Representations from Partially Paired, Small-Scale Data
items.summary: Modeling multimodal data from partially paired samples is critical for advancing domains like biomedicine, where vast unimodal datasets and foundation models exist but paired data remains scarce. Existing fusion methods rely on large-scale paired datasets, limiting their use in scenarios with incomplete pairing. We introduce CAMEO, an adversarial learning-based modality fusion framework that integrates modalities from small, partially paired datasets. Combining any pre-trained unimodal encoder with a cross-modal latent alignment mechanism, CAMEO learns shared representations requiring only minimal paired samples. Evaluated on computational pathology tasks such as niche classification and…

items.title: Foundation Model and Radiomics Distance Scores for Post-Hoc Segmentation Failure Detection
items.summary: Medical image segmentation models can fail silently when clinical data differs from training data. Deployed models rarely ship with quality control, and are often black boxes. Prior methods that work in this post-hoc failure detection setting still need a separate regression or segmentation model, registration, or access to model internals. We instead propose two failure scores based on the Mahalanobis distance to a labeled reference set. The first uses radiomic shape features of the predicted mask. The second uses frozen foundation model (FM) features, made mask-aware by overlaying the mask on the image, encoding it with a frozen DINOv3, and pooling patch features with more weight on the…

items.title: Constraints on ultralight dark matter couplings from orbital perturbations of binary pulsars
items.summary: Ultralight dark matter coupled directly to ordinary matter perturbs the orbits of binary pulsars, and the perturbation grows secularly when its frequency matches a harmonic of the orbital motion. We use this effect to constrain three couplings with the wideband timing data for the $50$ binary pulsars of the NANOGrav 15 yr data set: a linear and a quadratic universal coupling of a scalar field to matter, and a vector field coupled to baryon minus lepton number ($B-L$). For every system and for masses between $10^{-23}$ and $10^{-18}\,$eV, we build the timing signature from the perturbed orbital elements. We then sample the coupling together with the local amplitude, phase and direction of…

items.title: Effect of dark matter and scalar-cut potential on the macroscopic properties of neutron stars: A chiral quark mean field approach
items.summary: We investigate the effects of fermionic dark matter (DM) and scalar-cut potential ($U_{\text{cut}}(φ)$) on the equation of state (EOS) and macroscopic properties of neutron stars. The baryonic matter consists of neutrons, protons, electrons, and muons under the $β$-equilibrium and is described within the chiral SU(3) quark mean-field (CQMF) model. In this framework, quarks are confined within baryons, whose properties are modified through the exchange of scalar fields $σ$, $ζ$, and $δ$, and vector fields $ω$ and $ρ$. The DM is modelled as a self-interacting fermionic fluid with scalar $\varphi_D$ and vector $V_D^μ$ mediators. The baryonic and DM fluids interact only through gravity and are…

items.title: Time Series Foundation Models on the Edge
items.summary: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) forecast zero-shot with accuracy exceeding that of task-specific models, and the smaller ones fit on edge devices. Operational deployments must refresh their forecast as new observations arrive, and privacy and latency requirements often force this refresh onto resource-constrained edge devices. To serve as a forecasting system there, a TSFM must refresh quickly, keep latency and peak memory bounded as the stream grows, and retain its accuracy as the observed history accumulates. Refreshing incrementally without altering the forecast requires temporal causality: non-causal models recompute at every update, causal attention admits a KV cache that grows…

items.title: Impact of Topology and Sequence Length on the Pressure-Dependent Collapsibility of Proteins
items.summary: Several physical and evolutionary factors, including temperature, pressure, solvent quality, and natural selection, influence how amino acid sequences adopt their native structures. Although protein folding has been extensively studied, the physical determinants of protein collapse and their relationship to native-state folding remain less understood. In particular, "collapsibility", the intrinsic propensity of a protein sequence to form compact conformations, is distinct from but closely related to "foldability", the ability to reach the native structure. Previous theoretical studies suggested that collapsibility is encoded in native-state topology, potentially reflecting evolutionary…

items.title: HEART: Hierarchical Expert Adaptive Refinement Transformer for ECG Representation Learning
items.summary: Learning robust representations from electrocardiograms (ECGs) is challenging because repeated cardiac cycles coexist with subtle and sparse diagnostic cues in local morphology and rhythm-level context. Existing ECG foundation models commonly rely on Transformerbased patch encoders with uniformly shared dense refinement pathways, limiting adaptive processing across heterogeneous ECG tokens. We propose HEART (Hierarchical Expert Adaptive Refinement Transformer), an ECG foundation model that introduces stage-specific conditional expert refinement during self-supervised pre-training. HEART places a local-level MoE over patch-level representations before temporal contextualization and a…

items.title: A New Perspective on ANN-to-SNN Conversion: Hardware-Aligned Multi-Threshold Neuron Dynamics for Neuromorphic Inference
items.summary: By accumulating spikes over multiple timesteps, rate coding approximates the real-valued activations of an ANN, a principle that underpins numerous ANN-to-SNN conversion methods. However, the converted SNNs typically incur loss in accuracy compared to the original ANN. Existing methods either increase a number of timesteps or introduce more complex neuronal dynamics to reduce this accuracy gap. Yet, both approaches ultimately lead to the same outcome: redundancy either in information or in computation, thereby suffering from efficiency degradation. items.title: Innata-0: A Native Embodied World System with Model-Agent Co-Design
items.summary: The physical world is open-ended, dynamic, and partially observable. While foundation models have advanced embodied intelligence, standalone models struggle with long-horizon execution, and simply integrating models with agents may lead to inconsistencies between planning and physical control. To support reliable and adaptive behaviors in the physical world, we introduce Innata-0, a native embodied world system. Innata-0 jointly designs an embodied world-action model and an agent to combine their complementary strengths. The model, Innata-0-WAM, adopts a tri-tower Mixture-of-Transformers architecture that integrates understanding, prediction, and action generation. The agent,…

items.title: What Field Enumeration Costs to Compile in C++26: Native Reflection, Structured-Binding Packs, Reflection Libraries and Hand-Written Serializers on GCC 16
items.summary: C++26 adds standard ways to enumerate a struct's fields, among them static reflection (P2996, with P3394 annotations) and structured-binding packs (P1061), alongside hand-written code, X-macros and libraries (Boost.PFR, reflect-cpp, Glaze) that now ship pre-C++26 and C++26 paths. items.title: Responsible AI in human resource management: a sustainable framework for employee trust and organisational performance
items.summary: Purpose This paper examines how responsible artificial intelligence (AI) governance in human resource management (HRM) may support employee trust and sustainable organisational performance. Design/methodology/approach A conceptual model, developed through purposive theoretical synthesis, connects employee-visible governance with justice, focal trust, employee responses and organisational outcomes, while specifying contextual conditions and learning feedback. items.summary: As AI becomes embedded in organizational decision-making and knowledge production, employees gain new tools for accessing and generating information while also confronting concerns about algorithmic evaluation, data use, and accountability. Drawing on research on AI ethics, algorithmic management, and organizational creativity, this conceptual study defines organizational AI ethics governance as the rules, procedures, and allocation of responsibilities that guide the development, deployment, operation, and retirement of AI systems. items.title: Transformations of Managerial Leadership in the Era of Generative AI in Decision Making, Accountability, and Strategic Capability Development
items.summary: The rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence (generative AI) has significantly transformed how organizations manage information, develop strategic alternatives, and support managerial decision-making, shifting leadership responsibilities from information gathering toward directing, evaluating, and integrating AI-generated outputs. items.summary: Foundation models (FMs) are transforming artificial intelligence by generating large-scale representations of data that can be adapted across diverse downstream tasks. In computational pathology, the emergence of FMs trained on whole-slide images (WSIs) promises to reduce annotation burden, improve generalization, and enable multimodal disease modeling. This review summarizes the evolution in AI and deep learning that enabled pathology FM and surveys major publicly reported models developed by both academia and industry. items.title: Junction‐Programmed Excitability Control in a Thin‐Film Bipolar Neuromorphic Transistor
items.summary: Control of neuronal excitability is central to adaptive neuromorphic hardware, yet device‐defined states are often represented as synaptic quantities before being translated into neuronal activity. Junction‐defined excitability is demonstrated here in a thin‐film bipolar neuromorphic transistor, where distinct emitter–base (E–B) conditions directly regulate the membrane‐driving current and spike generation under fixed leaky‐integrate‐and‐fire parameters, without an intermediate synaptic‐weight representation. items.title: Yapay Zeka: Sadece Bir Yardımcı mı, Yoksa Geleceğin İş Gücü mü?
items.summary: Bu çalışma, yapay zeka teknolojilerinin günümüzdeki komut odaklı yardımcı araç rolünden gelecekteki otonom iş gücü ve karar mekanizmalarına evrimini incelemektedir. Contemporary AI research has demonstrated the remarkable effectiveness of large-scale neural networks, computational scaling, optimization, and increasingly sophisticated training procedures. items.summary: Cercospora is a widespread and destructive genus of fungi that causes leaf spot diseases on many economically important crops, including pulses, cereals, oilseeds, and vegetables. Global crop losses from these pathogens typically range between 50% and 75%. This review brings together evidence on taxonomy, diversity, morphology, host range, epidemiology, host–pathogen interactions and management options. items.title: Real-time neuromorphic audio and vision perception for autonomous robotic applications: Integration and experimental evaluation on a rover platform
items.summary: Neuromorphic sensing and computing offer a promising alternative to conventional deep learning pipelines for mobile robots, where perception must run continuously under tight latency and energy constraints. However, most neuromorphic solutions are still evaluated offline or on isolated benchmarks, and their integration into complete robotic systems remains largely unexplored. In this technical report, a four-wheel rover platform is presented that combines three real-time perception pipelines: a classical audio tagging pipeline based on Pretrained Audio Neural Networks (PANNs) running on an NVIDIA Jetson GPU, a neuromorphic audio pipeline in which a spiking neural network (SNN) is deployed…

items.title: BioEmu2: Scalable Emulation of Biomolecular Dynamics
items.summary: Despite major advances in structure prediction, modelling the motions and interactions that drive biomolecular function at scale remains a central challenge. We introduce BioEmu2, a generative model for atomically resolved biomolecular structures combining static structure prediction, equilibrium sampling and time evolution, that samples orders of magnitude faster than molecular dynamics (MD). Trained on experimental and synthetic structures and extensive MD data, it supports multi-component systems containing proteins, nucleic acids, modified residues, ligands and ions. Structure-prediction accuracy is comparable to top open-weight biomolecular folding models, and a context parallel mode…

items.title: Interpretable Tissue Architecture Complements Pathology Foundation Models
items.summary: Tissue architecture provides important information for histopathological assessment, yet its complementary predictive value alongside pathology foundation-model representations remains insufficiently understood. This study investigates whether interpretable measurements of cellular and multicellular tissue organization provide additional predictive information beyond learned representations. We introduce a 139-dimensional cellular-to-community representation comprising nine feature groups characterizing nuclear morphology, cellular composition, spatial connectivity, community organization, and cell-cell interactions. items.title: LesionAgent: Training-Free Agentic Tumor Tracking and Response Assessment in Longitudinal CT
items.summary: Every few months, a cancer patient's CT scans decide whether treatment continues. 3D foundation models can now detect, segment, register and track lesions, yet none of them reads the scans as a radiologist does. A radiologist decides which findings are lesions, which are the same lesion months later and whether a new spot means progression, and checks each decision against the extensive rules of a clinical guideline. We introduce LesionAgent, an LLM agent that performs this read end to end without task-specific training. It operates frozen 3D models as tools, acts in 3D through coordinate-labelled views, remembers every lesion across visits in a registry, verifies every model output it…

items.title: Magnetic-Field Response of a Hyperbolic Kitaev Spin Liquid
items.summary: Hyperbolic geometry can give rise to Kitaev spin liquids with distinct flux structures and Majorana spectra, raising the question of how these fractionalized states respond beyond exactly solvable limits. We address this question on the Kekulé-colored hyperbolic {8,3} lattice by developing an infinite projected entangled-pair-state approach with flux-resolved loop-gas initialization and geometry-adapted tensor-network contraction. Under uniform and staggered [111] magnetic fields, we find markedly different many-body responses. items.title: Neural Defend ARCAS 290M: A Robust Foundation Model for AI-Generated Audio Detection
items.summary: Voice cloning now needs only seconds of audio, and detectors tuned to one dataset often fail when the generator, channel, or language changes. We introduce ARCAS 290M, Neural Defend's foundation model for detecting AI-generated audio. A single frozen production model, with no benchmark-specific fine-tuning, generalizes across text-to-speech, voice-conversion, and codec-language-model generators, telephone and Bluetooth channels, recording conditions, and languages. We evaluate it on the complete official test sets of ten public benchmarks, scoring every recording exactly as released, and against commercial systems on independent leaderboards. ARCAS 290M ranks first among all systems on the…

items.title: Search-RSI: Expanding Search Worlds Along Multimodal Agents' Capability Frontier
items.summary: Multimodal search agents answer knowledge intensive visual questions by grounding them in retrieved evidence, and recent recipes train them on multi hop tasks that are synthesized from knowledge graphs and grown online to keep pace with the agent. These recipes, however, treat the searchable world as fixed: a new question can be well formed and verifiable while its evidence is absent from the retrieval backend, so the agent issues the right query, retrieves nothing, and is penalized as if its policy were at fault. Such unreachable negatives accumulate with every round of growth. We propose Search-RSI, a recursive self improvement framework that expands the search world along the agent's…

items.title: AutoOntologyBench: A Task-Grounded Benchmark for Agentic Knowledge Engineering
items.summary: Foundation-model agents are increasingly extending beyond software engineering (SWE) into autonomous scientific research, where acquiring and integrating domain knowledge remains a critical challenge. Recent industrial advances have increasingly adopted knowledge graphs and ontology-based semantic layers to organize heterogeneous knowledge into reusable representations. We ask: Can autonomous agents construct ontologies that help them solve real tasks, and do they offer measurable benefits over alternative knowledge representations? Existing benchmarks evaluate ontology correctness or agent task success in isolation, leaving the value of autonomously acquired knowledge unresolved. We…

items.title: Do Alice and Bob Dream of the Oracle? Wishful Cryptanalysis
items.summary: For two millennia, offense and defense have forged cryptographic security boundaries. Tools automated calculation and search, while humans drove discovery. Foundation models now mark a shift from automated computation to intelligent scientific discovery. Because cryptanalysis rests on exact mathematical definitions and immediately executable truth, it offers a proving ground for autonomous intelligence to move past security reliant on scarce human attention and explore structures beyond human working memory. Unguided models stall between two opposite traps: authority hallucination, where they surrender whenever prior literature declares a route blocked, and reasoning hallucination, where…

items.title: Embodied-Harness: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: Vision-language model (VLM)-based agents offer a promising approach to robotic manipulation, yet remain limited by inadequate memory organization, uncertain failure attribution, and limited reuse of execution experience. We propose Embodied-Harness, a dual-agent framework that improves manipulation by refining the execution harness without updating model parameters. The Actor interacts with the environment through a robot-control interface, while the Reflector converts execution evidence into reusable operational guidance. Hierarchical Memory Architecture maintains short-term execution context and long-term experiential knowledge to support execution and reflection. Evidence-based…

items.title: Learning in Symbiosis: Heterogeneous Federated Learning with ANNs and SNNs
items.summary: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs), widely regarded as the third generation of neural networks, represent a promising neuromorphic computing paradigm with the potential to reduce the energy footprint of Artificial Intelligence (AI). Their en-ergy efficiency makes SNNs particularly attractive for resource-constrained Edge AI devices, motivating growing research interest in Federated Learning (FL) with SNNs. Despite these advantages, integrating SNNs into existing FL systems remains challenging, as replacing all conventional Artificial Neural Network (ANN) devices with SNN-based alternatives is impractical. items.title: Adapting AI Weather Foundation Models to a Changing Climate
items.summary: AI weather foundation models learn from historical archives, while the climate distribution encountered during deployment continues to evolve. This growing model--climate mismatch motivates continual adaptation without repeated full-model retraining, but the structure of weather forecast errors determines how such adaptation should be performed. We develop an online adaptation framework that exploits two complementary error structures: geographically persistent biases and flow-dependent errors that vary with the atmospheric state. items.title: S-BFM: A Behavioral Foundation Model for Humanoid Control from Sparse Spatiotemporal Goals
items.summary: General-purpose whole-body trackers can execute diverse humanoid motions, but they require dense reference trajectories. However, tasks usually specify only where, in which posture, and when the robot should arrive, leaving the motion in between to a separate planner. Inspired by human motor coordination, our key idea is that a low-level controller can organize the intervening motion and its pace by itself from sparse goals with arrival times. In this paper, we propose S-BFM, a novel behavioral foundation model superior in its autonomy: it generates whole-body transitions from target postures, poses, and arrival times alone. items.title: From Tokens to Pixels: Training-Free Guided Upsampling of Frozen CARL Features for Hyperspectral Imaging
items.summary: Camera-agnostic foundation models such as CARL map spectral images from arbitrary sensors into a shared feature space, but deliver their features only on a token grid at one eighth of the input resolution. The usual bilinear interpolation blurs material boundaries over about one token and rounds off corners. We investigate how much spatial accuracy image-guided upsampling recovers for frozen CARL features without training the encoder or the upsampler. We compare joint bilateral upsampling (JBU), a guided filter and the pretrained AnyUp, each with the hyperspectral image or an RGB rendering as the guide. items.title: EchoAlign: Echocardiography foundation model with multilevel report alignment
items.summary: Echocardiography assesses the structure and function of the heart. Cardiologists read each study across several standard views and report the findings visible in those views by cardiac structure. AI foundation models can learn to analyze these studies from clinical reports, reducing annotation burden and supporting clinical interpretation. However, existing models are trained by pairing each video with the full clinical report, including structures and findings its view does not show. This mismatch lets a model associate a finding with incidental or spurious signals rather than its visual evidence, which limits accuracy, anatomical grounding and clinical trust. items.title: NavRSI: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement for Vision-and-Language Navigation
items.summary: Frontier large language models (LLMs) have enabled vision-and-language navigation (VLN) through direct closed-loop perception and action. However, navigation performance depends strongly on the harness governing LLM-environment interactions, while existing harnesses largely rely on manually designed navigation tools, memory, and agent roles. items.summary: The EU Artificial Intelligence Act (AI Act) imposes detailed obligations on providers of high-risk AI systems but offers limited operational guidance, particularly when these systems integrate third-party General-Purpose AI (GPAI) models. This paper introduces a toolkit that fosters the development of legal-by-design AI-assisted recruitment systems by translating the core legal obligations of the AI Act's conformity assessment---specifically Articles 9--15 and Annex IV---into techno-normative requirements and corresponding guiding questions. items.summary: We introduce Transformation Tracking and Understanding (TTU), extending video object tracking to environments where objects undergo physical assemblies and disassemblies. TTU requires continuously tracking objects through transformations, identifying new entities, maintaining a state graph of their relationships, and assigning semantic labels to transformations. While foundation models (e.g., SAM 2/3) maintain tracklets through appearance changes, they cannot update semantic identities as objects physically evolve. items.title: Regularizing gravity in the presence of matter fields
items.summary: We investigate how matter fields affect spacetime regularity in a class of gravitational theories with second-order field equations in spherical symmetry, of which general relativity is a special case, and which may encode effective corrections from an underlying quantum theory of gravity. Focusing on spherically symmetric black holes and cosmological spacetimes in theories in which vacuum spacetimes display bounded curvature invariants, we derive the conditions under which regular geometries can be supported by static and perturbative scalar fields, electromagnetic fields, and radiation fluids. items.title: Latent Jacobian Steer: Eliciting Contact-Rich Out-of-Distribution Behaviors from Pretrained Humanoid Controllers
items.summary: Given a pretrained general latent-conditioned whole-body humanoid controller, say a behavioral foundation model (BFM), how can we elicit complex and contact-rich out-of-distribution behaviors? Raw joint-action exploration enables direct, task-specific adjustments but can disrupt coordination learned by the pretrained controller, whereas latent exploration retains that coordination but is difficult to steer toward desired physical effects. items.summary: Optical cavities are widely used in atomic physics experiments to control the spatial geometry and spectral properties of atom-light interactions. Recently, an optical lattice generated by the pristine mode of an optical cavity was utilized to hold and extend the quantum coherence of atomic spatial superpositions. Here, we describe an in-vacuum optical cavity designed to enhance the spatial and temporal coherence of optical lattice atom interferometers to one millimeter wavepacket separations and one minute measurement durations. items.summary: Understanding how spiking neural networks (SNNs) efficiently process data streams is key to (i) studying how biological brains conserve energy for lifelong predictions and (ii) enabling efficient continuous AI inference. In this work, we propose a theory on how an SNN incrementally tracks its corresponding firing-rate network, a continuous-valued neural network (ANN). items.title: InterBand-EMG: A Cross-Band Foundation Model for Generalizable Hand-Pose Estimation
items.summary: Surface electromyography (sEMG) enables continuous hand-pose estimation, but learning representations that generalize across users and movements remains challenging. items.title: SIR-Agent: Skill-Augmented Image Restoration Agent with Recursive Self-Improvement
items.summary: Agents for Image Restoration (IR) aim to leverage Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to autonomously perceive image degradation and invoke IR tools. items.title: Stratum: A Hardware-Software Co-Design Framework for SNN Inference on RISC-V
items.summary: Efficient spiking neural network (SNN) inference on RISC-V processors requires tracing implementation costs back to the compiler and hardware decisions that produce them. items.summary: Based on current observational data, there is a strong possibility that dark energy was in a phantom regime in the near past, and a transition from a phantom to a quintessential regime may have occurred. items.title: ECG-LabWAS: A Laboratory-Wide Association Study Using a Fine-Tuned Single-Lead Electrocardiogram Foundation Model

items.title: Neural Defend Ranks #1 in Global Audio Deepfake Detection Benchmark - ARCAS on the Podonos Independent Leaderboard

items.title: A Frugal AI Framework for India: Responsible and Right-sized AI

items.title: BusemannFormer: Horospherical Self-Attention for Hyperbolic Graph Transformers
items.summary: Hyperbolic neural networks excel on hierarchical graph data, yet existing hyperbolic Transformers largely adapt conventional attention without explicitly exploiting the ideal boundary, a geometric structure closely tied to tree hierarchy. items.summary: Foundation models have advanced SAR image interpretation but created a heterogeneous, fragmented model ecosystem. items.title: Paper IV — Immune-Gated Recursive Self-Improvement (IG-RSI), Acquired Cognitive Immunity & Tritemporal K-Time Consolidation
items.summary: Conventional neural language models are epistemically static after deployment: either their parameters remain permanently frozen—forcing all adaptation into external retrieval databases (RAG / GraphDB) and brittle system prompts—or they undergo naive continual fine-tuning that rapidly degrades through model collapse, template overgeneralization, and self-reinforcing hallucination. In this paper, we formulate a biological and systems-engineering alternative: Immune-Gated Recursive Self-Improvement (IG-RSI). We propose that genuine neural evolution requires pairing recursive weight consolidation with an Acquired Cognitive Immune System—an adaptive internal defense architecture that…

items.title: Emotional Superintelligence: A New Paradigm for Compassionate Artificial Intelligence
items.summary: Artificial Intelligence has achieved significant advances in perception, language generation, reasoning, and decision-making. However, current Artificial Intelligence systems primarily optimize task performance and remain limited in their ability to account for emotional context, ethical considerations, and long-term human well-being. Existing research on Emotional Intelligence, Affective Computing, Compassionate Artificial Intelligence and Theory of Mind addresses different aspects of this challenge, but these capabilities have largely been studied independently. We propose Emotional Superintelligence as a new computational paradigm that integrates contextual emotional understanding,…

Building on TKQB01 (Quantum Neurolinguistics), it analyses how high-LET particles threaten three candidate mechanisms — π-electron delocalisation in aromatic residues, low-barrier proton tunnelling, and Fröhlich-type coherent oscillations — and ranks their expected fragility. Five falsifiable space-medicine hypotheses (S1–S5) and a three-gate ground-based experimental roadmap are presented, designed for existing heavy-ion facilities and neural organoid platforms. The central thesis of the MVL posits that the most efficient locus of systemic change lies not at the smallest or largest scale, but at an…

items.title: DC-Debates: Difficulty-Calibrated Debate Transcripts as Stimuli for Scalable Oversight Research with Human Participants
items.summary: Approaches to scalable oversight involving human judges, such as AI safety via debate, will be more likely to achieve success if systematic errors in judgment can be minimized. Research on approaches to reducing this error, such as different ways of aggregating participant judgments or manipulating instructions to human participants, is more likely to generalise well if conducted using stimuli analogous to the kinds of stimuli that we expect strong trained AI debaters to generate. This requires well-designed transcripts that are difficult enough to leave room for interventions to improve judge accuracy, but tractable enough that an attentive judge has some hope of arriving at the correct…

items.title: When measurements of AI systems disagree A methodological review of dissociations in AI safety
items.summary: Abstract Artificial intelligence safety research compares systems' answers and actions with output probabilities, generated reasoning, internal activations and monitoring judgments. These measurements can disagree about what a system knows, what influenced its response and whether unwanted behavior occurred. This critical tutorial review organizes the emerging literature around five comparisons: relative sensitivity, incremental value, functional dissociation, causal intervention and targeted robustness. Worked examples distinguish reported findings, their inferential limits and informative follow-up comparisons. The comparisons are introduced through simpler settings and then applied…

items.title: A multimodal foundation model for molecular and morphologic data in oncology.
items.summary: Foundation models are advancing computational pathology by transferring knowledge from large datasets to diagnostic, prognostic and treatment response tasks. Most existing models, however, either operate at the patch level or learn slide-level representations using image-based objectives, coarse tissue labels or pathology reports that vary across institutions and reflect the subjectivity inherent in narrative reporting. Here we introduce THREADS, which instead learns general-purpose whole-slide representations by aligning tissue morphology with genomic or transcriptomic profiles. THREADS was pretrained on over 47,000 hematoxylin-and-eosin-stained tissue sections and evaluated across 107…

items.title: The Impact of Hurricane Helene on the Incidence of Acute Gastrointestinal Illness in North Carolina, US: A Controlled Interrupted Time Series Analysis
items.summary: In September 2024, Hurricane Helene caused significant flooding in western North Carolina (NC), leading to concerns surrounding water quality, including the risk of acute gastrointestinal illness (AGI). The potential for flooding-related drinking water contamination is exacerbated for private well users, who comprised a large proportion of the population most affected by the hurricane. Here we investigated the impact of Hurricane Helene on AGI and determined if this impact was different in areas with greater proportions of residents using private wells. We used electronic health records from Truveta to identify inpatient and outpatient visits to hospitals for AGI in NC from 2016-2024 at…

items.title: A report-supervised EEG-language foundation model enables broad, interactive clinical interpretation
items.summary: Medical AI for complex signals such as electroencephalography (EEG) relies on costly expert annotations and predefined diagnostic labels that fail to capture the richness and nuance of clinical interpretation. Whether models trained on routine clinical reports can overcome these limitations while matching expert-supervised performance remains unclear. We introduce EEG Copilot, a biosignal-language foundation model trained on routine EEG-report pairs without dedicated task-specific expert annotations. Across two external datasets (6,078 EEGs), EEG Copilot performed on par with a state-of-the-art expert-supervised model across 11 shared findings (mean AUROC 0.80-0.81), corroborated by direct…

items.title: The ITE-Transformer: A pre-trained foundation model for predicting individualized treatment effects from electronic health records
items.summary: Transformer-based foundation models have shown strong potential for modeling longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs), yet existing models focus primarily on risk prediction rather than treatment effect estimation, which limits evidence generation. Here, we introduce the ITE-Transformer, a transformer-based framework that combines self-supervised representation learning from longitudinal patient trajectories with doubly robust causal machine learning for predicting individualized treatment effects (ITEs). As a result, our ITE-Transformer allows to study counterfactual questions of how an individual patient's outcome may differ under alternative treatment strategies. The…

items.title: Retinal foundation-model versus ImageNet pretraining for deep learning grading of diabetic retinopathy: an external validation study
items.summary: Abstract Purpose To determine whether retinal foundation-model pretraining reduces the loss of diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading agreement on external fundus-photograph datasets compared with ImageNet-pretrained convolutional networks. Methods RETFound (linear probe and full fine-tuning), EfficientNet-B3 and ResNet-50 were developed on APTOS 2019 (3,662 images) and tested unchanged on Messidor-2 (1,744 images, adjudicated grades) and IDRiD (516 images). The prespecified primary outcome was the difference in internal-to-external quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) drop relative to EfficientNet-B3 for one training run per model; a post hoc analysis averaged three or four runs per model. Results…

items.title: MammoInsight: A Unified Multi-Task Deep Learning Framework for Mammography Analysis
items.summary: Abstract Background Mammography interpretation requires simultaneous assessment of multiple clinical attributes such as cancer status, breast density, BI-RADS score, abnormality type, and molecular subtype. The existing AI systems generally address these tasks in isolation, limiting clinical utility and generalizability. Methods We present MammoInsight, a unified multi-task deep learning framework built on MedImageInsight foundation model backbone, incorporating SAM-Med2D-guided region-of-interest pooling, cross-view attention fusion across both standard mammography views, weighted ordinal regression for ordered clinical labels, DHN-NCE contrastive regularisation, and homoscedastic…

items.title: Continual learning in oncology AI: A framework for safe clinical translation.
items.summary: AI models remain largely static, yet cancer care never stands still. Evolution of scanning technology, imaging protocols, staging criteria, therapies, and patient populations can silently erode model performance and patient safety. Continual learning (CL) enables models to continuously acquire new knowledge, while minimizing catastrophic forgetting. Here, we review CL methods and their oncology applications, predominantly in imaging and pathology, and discuss CL as an option for maintaining foundation models, alongside recalibration and retraining. We examine translational barriers, including hidden regressions in underrepresented populations, label and concept drift, privacy constraints…

items.title: Probing Kaniadakis Holographic Dark Energy in a Bianchi Type-V Self-Creation Universe: Dynamics and Diagnostics
items.summary: Abstract We study a spatially homogeneous and anisotropic Bianchi type-V universe in Barber’s second self-creation theory of gravitation, filled with pressureless dark matter and an anisotropic Kaniadakis holographic dark energy (KHDE) fluid with a Hubble-horizon cutoff. We show that the off-diagonal field equation forces the two skewness parameters of the dark-energy fluid to be equal and opposite, δ = −γ, so that a fluid with two equal principal pressures is necessarily isotropic. Moreover, the vanishing-trace condition often used to integrate the scalar-field equation is equivalent to a vanishing Ricci scalar and over-determines the system; instead, we integrate the scalar-field…

items.title: Phase separation in cell-extracellular matrix adhesion: looking back and moving forward.
items.summary: The exponential growth of phase separation research has uncovered fundamental concepts across biology, making it timely to reassess findings across fields. Here, we summarise advances linking biomolecular condensation to integrin-mediated cell-extracellular matrix adhesion and migration. We discuss how adhesion proteins undergoing phase separation may regulate adhesion properties across the adhesion life cycle, including integrin clustering, nascent adhesion assembly, maturation, dynamics, and stability. We also highlight recent discoveries showing that biomolecular condensates can transiently sequester adhesion components following acute adhesion disassembly. We further discuss the roles…

items.title: Bacterial Hsp90 and its interacting partners.
items.summary: Protein quality control depends on molecular chaperones to promote protein folding, remodeling, disaggregation, and degradation. The major families of chaperones present in nearly all organisms are Hsp90, Hsp70, Hsp60, and Clp/Hsp100. Here, we review Hsp90 chaperones with particular emphasis on bacterial Hsp90s. Unlike eukaryotic Hsp90, the bacterial Hsp90 is independent of Hsp90 cochaperones and thus provides a simpler and more accessible system to study the mechanism of action of Hsp90. Despite this simplicity, bacterial Hsp90s are highly homologous to eukaryotic family members and exhibit sensitivity to the same small-molecule inhibitors as eukaryotic Hsp90. Thus, insights gained from…

items.title: Stability and tethering of the preconoidal rings in Toxoplasma gondii.
items.summary: Apicomplexan parasites rely on a specialized apical cytoskeleton to generate the forces required for motility and host-cell invasion. At its core lies the conoid, composed of spiraling tubulin fibers capped by three preconoidal rings (PCRs), which anchor the actin nucleator Formin 1 and contribute to force transmission at the parasite apex. Here, we refine the molecular organization and function of the PCRs in Toxoplasma gondii. We show that PCR composition and stability change during parasite maturation, with a subset of PCR proteins, Pcr2 and Pcr3, adopting a characteristic half-ring organization. We identify MyoL, a divergent pseudomyosin, as a previously unrecognized PCR component.…

items.title: Identification of SAMD4B as a Centrosome-Associated Regulator of the Sonic Hedgehog Signaling Pathway
items.summary: Background: Many protein-protein interactions are required for the assembly and function of primary cilia, microtubule-based organelles critical for the Sonic hedgehog (Shh) signaling pathway and, in turn, for embryonic development and tissue homeostasis. However, our understanding of this complex process remains incomplete. Methods: To identify new regulators of primary cilia formation or function, we carried out proximity labeling experiments and compared interactomes under ciliogenesis-restrictive and permissive conditions. Using an unbiased strategy, we selected candidates that were tested functionally by siRNA-mediated depletion or gene editing, in combination with gene expression…

items.title: A developmental resource mapping tubulin isotype deployment during corneal morphogenesis.
items.summary: Microtubules are core cytoskeletal polymers that support epithelial organization, polarity, and tissue morphogenesis. They are composed of α- and β-tubulin heterodimers encoded by multigene families that generate closely related but distinct isotypes. Although several tubulin isotypes have been implicated in ocular development and disease, their spatial organization during corneal morphogenesis remains poorly defined. Here we establish a resource for visualizing and quantifying tubulin isotype localization during corneal development using the chick embryo. Comparative amino acid sequence analysis demonstrates that chick and human α- and β-tubulin isotypes are highly conserved within…

items.title: Drosophila Orb2 contributes to neural stem cell centrosome asymmetry and cell growth.
items.summary: The deregulation of neural stem cell (NSC) homeostasis underlies neurodevelopmental disorders and tumorigenesis. In the Drosophila larval brain, NSCs divide asymmetrically along an invariant apical-basal axis to yield a larger self-renewing stem cell and a smaller, differentiating sibling. NSC divisions are instructed by centrosomes, which recruit pericentriolar material (PCM) important for microtubule-organizing activity. During interphase, NSC centrosomes are defined by asymmetries in PCM composition and functional activity. These asymmetries help align the mitotic spindle and position the cleavage furrow. Here, we show that the conserved RNA-binding protein Orb2 is required to enrich…

items.title: Neuromorphic self-aware wings for embodied-intelligent bionic flying microrobotics.
items.summary: Flying insects achieve robust proprioception and agile flight control using distributed mechanoreceptors on their wings, but current bionic flying microrobots rely heavily on external sensors for state monitoring. Typical sensing solutions including offboard vision or surface-mounted devices inevitably sacrifice either flight autonomy or payload capacity. Inspired by insect wing mechanoreception, we introduce an embodied neuromorphic self-sensing paradigm that eliminates this tradeoff by enabling intrinsic, aerodynamics-maintenance proprioception in flapping-wing systems. Instead of treating the wing solely as a propulsive structure, we reengineer it into a self-contained sensory organ…

items.title: An all-magnonic neuron with tunable fading memory.
items.summary: Magnonics offers nanometer-scale wave propagation and strong nonlinearities, making it attractive for neuromorphic applications such as artificial neurons. Yet, magnonic elements with interconnections solely within the magnonic system remain challenging, preventing the realization of interconnected magnonic neurons to date. Here, we experimentally demonstrate an all-magnonic neuron that reacts to magnon inputs with thresholded, amplified magnon firing and subsequent self-reset, enabling all-magnonic operation and cascading. Our approach is based on micro-antenna excitation on an ultralow damping garnet with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, where we exploit the positive magnon frequency…

items.title: Monolayer h-BN RF Switch Toward Monolithic Inductor Switching in Wide-Tuning-Range LC-VCOs.
items.summary: Next-generation wireless systems demand monolithic three-dimensional (3D) system-on-chip architectures to overcome planar scaling limits and reduce interconnect delays. Realizing this back-end-of-line (BEOL) integration on complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) platforms requires ultracompact, high-performance radio-frequency (RF) switches. Here, we present a non-volatile RF switch based on a monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) memristor employing an Ag/h-BN/Ag structure. The device exhibits a low SET voltage of 1.11 V and stable endurance exceeding 500 cycles. At 20 GHz, it achieves an insertion loss of 0.81 dB and an isolation of 32.91 dB, enabled by a low on-resistance (R…

items.title: Growth-Spiral Control of Defect Topology and Local Vertical Piezoresponse in Bi4Ti3O12 Thin Films.
items.summary: Aurivillius phase materials are layered ferroelectrics with high thermal stability (>600 °C) and fatigue resistance, yet their polarization is predominantly in-plane, limiting integration into vertical device architectures relevant to future memory, data storage, and neuromorphic computing concepts. Achieving robust vertical polarization in these systems remains fundamentally challenging because of crystallographic symmetry constraints. Although defects can locally reorient polarization, deterministic control of defect topology through growth-mode engineering remains largely unexplored in layered ferroelectrics. Here, we demonstrate that precise control of nominal precursor loading and…

Bio-Based Materials for a Circular Economy: A Review of Advances, Barriers, and Pathways to Scalable Adoption
items.summary: The shift from a linear "take-make-dispose" industrial model toward a circular economy has made bio-based materials a central focus of sustainability research and policy.This paper presents a narrative literature review of recent advances in bio-based materials-mycelium-based composites, algae-derived bioplastics and polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHA), agricultural-waste-derived fibers, and bacterial cellulose-and evaluates their contribution to circular economy objectives.Records

items.title: MULTISPECIES CO-DESIGNING WITH FUNGI: DIGESTION, DISCARDS AND REPAIR
items.summary: This practice-based thesis proposes designing with fungi is a relational and emergent co-creative process. Located in the fields of critical biodesign and expanded fashion and textiles, the thesis examines the problem of standardisation, where growing mushroom mycelium materials to achieve homogenous products is, I argue, at odds with the flexible and indeterminate tendencies of fungal agents. Untethered from commercial imperatives, what emerges is an approach I term multispecies co-designing that foregrounds human and more-than-human relational exchanges across species difference. These transversal relations occur through experimentation in the studio-lab via shared material and…

Hyphal differentiation and cell wall remodeling in Trametes versicolor underlie a layered architecture in pure mycelium materials
items.summary: Background: Pure mycelium materials grown at the air-liquid interface are promising leather alternatives, yet they are generally treated as homogeneous sheets of fungal biomass. Because basidiomycetes differentiate their hyphae into generative, skeletal and ligative cell types, the properties of such materials may instead arise from an internal tissue organisation. In this study, cell types produced by the trimitic white-rot fungus Trametes versicolor during Liquid State Surface Fermentation were characterized and the impact of their spatial organisation, mechanics and cell wall composition on the resulting material was analysed.
