items.title: A new approach to fixed-time synchronization of spatiotemporal memristive neural networks with mixed time-varying delays.
items.summary: This paper addresses the fixed-time synchronization (FXTS) problems of spatiotemporal memristive neural networks with mixed delays and reaction-diffusion terms (MDRDMNNs) via aperiodically semi-intermittent switching control (ASISC). First, a novel fixed-time stability criterion based on the hyperbolic-cosine function is established, and an explicit upper bound estimation of the settling time is derived, thereby providing a new theoretical perspective for achieving system synchronization. Furthermore, leveraging the established fixed-time stability results and introducing the ASISC strategy, which exhibits distinct advantages in energy efficiency and cost reduction over continuous control,…

items.title: Brain-inspired low-rank spiking neural networks for aircraft control with manifold representation reinforcement learning.
items.summary: Achieving stable and rapid aircraft attitude control under flight uncertainty and external disturbance remains a challenging task. To address this problem, this paper proposes a manifold representation reinforcement learning framework based on a Low-rank recurrent spiking neural network (LRRSNN). The framework integrating biological plausibility of LRRSNN with manifold learning method leverages low-rank connectivity and small-world topology to improve the efficiency and robustness of controller. To enhance training stability, we design a geometric constraint mechanism that incorporates Riemannian gradient descent. It is shown that the attitude controller based on proposed framework…

items.title: Artificial Intelligence for Weed Detection in Precision Agriculture: A Review from Classical Machine Learning to Foundation Models
items.summary: Weeds are among the most significant biotic constraints to global agricultural production, causing annual crop losses exceeding US$48 billion, while the emergence of more than 500 herbicide-resistant weed biotypes has eroded the effectiveness of conventional management, particularly blanket herbicide application. This review, conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines, synthesises evidence from 117 peer-reviewed studies (2015–2026) across five major databases. Unlike prior reviews focused on a single imaging modality or technique, it provides a unified analysis spanning RGB, multispectral, hyperspectral, and satellite imagery together with classical machine learning, deep…

items.title: AnyVIO: Feed-Forward Streaming Visual-Inertial Odometry Across Platforms
items.summary: Geometric foundation models (GFMs) estimate camera mo- tion and scene structure from images without requiring ex- pert parameter tuning, but either lack metric scale or rely on learned priors to infer scale, which is unobservable from monocular images alone. Inertial sensing offers a way to observe metric scale, but existing methods add inertial in- formation through a filter or factor graph, which reintro- duces bespoke parameter tuning and optimization costs that can grow with the trajectory. To bridge this gap, we present AnyVIO, a real-time, feed-forward streaming model for monocular visual-inertial odometry (VIO), which combines a streaming GFM with an inertial foundation model (IFM).…

items.title: UV Bounds on Inflationary Parity Violation
items.summary: A question of fundamental interest is whether parity is violated on large scales in the Universe. This possibility has been motivated by recent analyses of the four-point matter correlation function. It has also been suggested that detectable parity violation could be generated during inflation by the dynamical Chern-Simons operator, a leading effective field theory correction to general relativity. In this work, we examine this possibility in realistic UV completions, including fermionic and string-theoretic examples. We show that existing bounds on the tensor-scalar-scalar (TSS) bispectrum strongly constrain the possibility of generating a detectable parity-odd trispectrum. For…

items.title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithm for Differential Equations: Application to Simulating a Biomolecular System
items.summary: Quantum algorithms for differential equations have the potential for substantial algorithmic speedups over classical methods. However, they rely on certain assumptions and abstract oracle specifications that leave their practical feasibility and computational advantages for realistic applications unclear. Here we formalize the concept of an end-to-end quantum algorithm for differential equations as one that accepts classical inputs and returns classical outputs, and provide implementations for algorithmic primitives in constructing such algorithms. We present a tailored end-to-end quantum algorithm for the linearized Poisson-Boltzmann (LPB) equation, a partial differential equation (PDE)…

items.title: Activity-driven motion and deformation of a circular membrane domain
items.summary: Lipid bilayer membranes are nanometer-thin fluid interfaces characterized by both in-plane fluidity and lateral compositional heterogeneity. Cholesterol-rich liquid domains ("lipid rafts") are thought to regulate the spatial organization of membrane proteins and numerous cellular processes. While the passive diffusion and equilibrium shape fluctuations of membrane domains are well understood, much less is known about how the activity of molecular machines, such as protein pumps and enzymes, influences their mobility and deformation. Here, we analyze the dynamics of a membrane domain driven by an embedded molecular machine within the framework of two-dimensional Stokes flow. The molecular…

items.title: Multi-institutional grading of Barrett's esophagus dysplasia without stain normalization using a pathology foundation model and multiple instance learning
items.summary: Barrett's esophagus dysplasia grading suffers substantial inter-observer variability, particularly for low-grade dysplasia, complicating clinical decision-making. We conducted a retrospective multi-institutional diagnostic accuracy study of a foundation model-based deep learning system for dysplasia grading, using 969 H\&E-stained whole slide images from four institutions. Patch-level classifiers trained on expert annotations identified diagnostically relevant regions, followed by attribute-aware multiple instance learning for slide-level classification as non-dysplastic Barrett's esophagus (NDBE), low-grade dysplasia, or high-grade dysplasia. On a held-out test set (n = 130),…

items.title: Refractive Neutrino Mass: Effects of Fluctuations of the Dark Matter Field
items.summary: Observed neutrino oscillations can be reproduced by a refractive neutrino mass-squared arising from interactions with ultralight scalar dark matter (ULDM). The wave behaviour of the scalar field gives rise to a fluctuating interference pattern, inducing spatial and temporal variations in the refractive mass that can distort neutrino oscillation probabilities. We simulate the interference patterns of the scalar field in the presence of self-interactions. Using results of these simulations, the oscillation probabilities for JUNO and T2K experiments are computed. We find that the refractive mass scenario remains viable for the complex scalar field without self-coupling for $m_φ\lesssim…

items.title: Higher cluster-tilting modules for blocks of finite groups
items.summary: We classify the $d$-representation-finite blocks of finite group algebras over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic. The main step is to show that if a block admits a $d$-cluster-tilting module with $d\geq3$, then it splits over the fraction field of the Witt vectors. This excludes generalized quaternion defect groups of order at least $16$.

items.title: Asuka-FM: A System-Architectural Co-Design Framework for Efficient Text-to-Image Pretraining on Consumer Hardware
items.summary: Frontier text-to-image (T2I) foundation models predominantly rely on multi-billion parameter Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) pretrained across massive compute clusters, creating an accessibility barrier for academic laboratories. When training DiTs from scratch on single consumer GPUs (e.g., an NVIDIA RTX 4090 with 24\,GB VRAM), practitioners encounter three primary bottlenecks: quadratic attention sequence costs, Just-In-Time (JIT) compilation graph breaks induced by variable aspect-ratio bucketing, and an autoencoder throughput wall where frozen Variational Autoencoder (VAE) operations dominate step latency. In this work, we introduce \textbf{Asuka-FM}, an end-to-end system and…

items.title: FEA solver integration of a composite World Model with a Spiking Neural Network memory Block for computationally efficient modelling of defects and variabilities
items.summary: Each fibre-reinforced composite structure has a unique material architecture. The manufacturing methods used and the presence of defects lead to local variations which require material-scale models that can resolve the response in real time at every location in the structure. Concurrent multi-scale schemes provide this capability, but at a prohibitive computational cost for large structures as the number of integration points and time increments scales with size. Surrogates have been studied extensively as replacements for material-scale models to mitigate these computational limitations. A surrogate must represent an arbitrary local architecture including defects, track the irreversible…

items.title: WeMM-Video: Pushing the Frontiers of Open-Source Omni-Modal Video Understanding
items.summary: Video understanding, particularly with accompanying audio, remains a central challenge in multimodal intelligence. In this report, we introduce \textbf{WeMM-Video}, a family of Chinese-English bilingual omni-modal foundation models spanning 2B, 4B, 9B, and 35B-A3B variants. Centering on joint audio-visual perception and reasoning, WeMM-Video unifies text, image, audio, and video processing within a hybrid-thinking paradigm, seamlessly supporting both a non-thinking instruct mode for fast, direct responses and a thinking mode for explicit step-by-step reasoning. The models are trained on a large-scale multimodal corpus of approximately 1.2 trillion tokens through progressive pre-training…

items.title: Classification of Chern-Simons Couplings and Deformed Pull-Backs on D-Branes
items.summary: We establish a framework for classifying higher-derivative Ramond-Ramond (RR) couplings on Dp-branes, focusing on the complete scattering amplitude of a closed-string RR state, a gauge field, and two transverse scalars. The low-energy expansion reveals infinite massless poles and local interaction terms, surpassing standard Myers and Taylor expansions. We propose a higher-class deformation of the pullback using mixed Chern-Simons transgression operators to address these complexities. Our three conjectures are as follows: 1. items.title: C-LiTE: A Lightweight Foundation Model for Cellular feature learning in Histopathology
items.summary: Characterising individual cells is fundamental to computational pathology, as cellular morphology informs tasks such as tumour grading, mitotic assessment and immune profiling. However, most pathology foundation models are trained on tissue patches and capture cellular features only implicitly, while existing cell-level models are either restricted to specific cell populations or rely on computationally expensive architectures with hundreds of millions of parameters. Applying ViTs directly to small cellular crops also presents an architectural challenge: upsampling increases computational cost without adding morphological information and may introduce interpolation artefacts. To address…

items.title: Exposure-Aware Informative Path Planning Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: This paper addresses the finite-budget exposure-aware informative path planning (IPP) problem for a fleet of mobile sensing agents. The agents map an unknown scalar field while limiting exposure to high field intensity. Existing IPP methods optimize informativeness under motion or resource constraints, but do not address field exposure constraints. We formulate exposure-aware IPP (EA-IPP) as a scalarized bi-objective belief-state Markov decision process that trades the normalized Gaussian-process (GP) information gain against a normalized measurement-derived fleet exposure index. A parameter-shared proximal policy optimization (PPO) framework with decentralized actors and a centralized…

items.title: All-Order Linearized Hydrodynamics of Charged Holographic Plasmas
items.summary: We investigate linearized all-order transport in a finite-density holographic plasma described by five-dimensional Einstein-Maxwell-Chern-Simons theory. By retaining the full frequency- and momentum-dependence of the fluid/gravity equations, we determine generalized shear, diffusion, higher-gradient, and chiral-vortical transport functions together with their real-time memory kernels. The different channels exhibit a clear hierarchy of temporal response: the leading shear and diffusion sectors respond promptly, whereas the higher-gradient sectors develop only after a finite buildup time. Remarkably, the chiral-vortical response also shows a finite buildup time despite entering at first…

items.title: Physics-Informed Feature Representations and Pretrained Tabular Foundation Models for Generalizable Melt Pool Geometry Prediction
items.summary: Developing generalizable, data-efficient machine learning (ML) models for advanced manufacturing remains challenging because experimental datasets are limited and process-property relationships vary across materials and operating conditions. In laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), melt pool width, depth, and melting mode (conduction, transition, or keyhole) govern process stability and defect formation. Conventional ML models typically use dimensional process parameters, which represent laser-material interactions only implicitly and may limit cross-material transfer. This study evaluates whether two physics-informed dimensionless features, normalized enthalpy and Peclet number, combining laser…

items.title: Two powers, one scalar field: unified early and late dark energy
items.summary: We investigate whether a single canonical scalar field can account for both early and late dark energy. We consider a double-power potential in which a steep positive-power term can generate an early peak in the scalar energy-density fraction, while an inverse-power term supports late-time acceleration. This evolution requires the steep term to dominate initially and become subdominant later. items.title: Notes on non-equilibrium thermodynamics of Robinson-Trautman spacetimes
items.summary: Robinson-Trautman spacetimes are determined by a parabolic heat-type evolution equation of fourth order for a scalar field on future null infinity. This equation may be re-written as an energy balance for an asymptotically time-like observer. In turn, it becomes a first law in the context of non-equilibrium thermodynamics if the non-linear memory is interpreted as heat. This leads to a local version of temperature and a manifestly increasing entropy density from the viewpoint of the environment.

items.title: When Foundation Models Disagree: Representational Heterogeneity for Calibrated Uncertainty in Whole-Slide Image Classification
items.summary: Pathology foundation models supply strong representations for whole-slide image classification, yet the confidence attached to their predictions remains hard to trust. Prevailing uncertainty estimators act within a single feature space and thereby overlook the uncertainty that the choice of foundation-model representation itself induces. This work introduces CALIFUSE, a calibration-oriented framework that fuses several pathology foundation models for the specific purpose of uncertainty estimation. items.title: Sage-Evolve-Preview:Adaptive Observation for Post-Training Self-Improvement
items.summary: Post-training recursive self-improvement (RSI) iteratively improves a target capability, operationalized by a fixed anchor benchmark, through repeated intervention, training, and evaluation. Yet most loops use the anchor's aggregate score as their sole observation, so early gains give way to stalled progress and repetitive exploration. When this anchor-only feedback ceases to reveal actionable gaps, a plateau may reflect an exhausted observation rather than an exhausted capability. We introduce adaptive observation (AdaObs), an observation-side mechanism of harness evolution that keeps the anchor objective fixed while adapting the active observation. items.title: High-Speed Widefield Hyperspectral Imaging
items.summary: Fourier-transform hyperspectral imaging is an emerging technology that combines widefield acquisition with flexible spectral resolution. Yet, it typically requires the acquisition of dense sequences of full-field interferograms during optical-path scanning, which ultimately reduces the final throughput. To circumvent this limitation, this manuscript introduces an event-based Fourier-transform hyperspectral microscopy technique that exploits the coupling of a neuromorphic event camera with a common-path birefringent interferometer operated under continuous scanning. Specifically, two complementary acquisition strategies are investigated, one with steady broadband illumination where the…

items.title: Controlling the Humanoid Robot H1-2 With a Simulated Biologically Plausible Network
items.summary: Artificial Spiking Neural Networks have gained remarkable attention in the last few years due to their proven ability in simulating biological neural cultures and producing similar activity and trends. Nevertheless, whether they can be trained for humanoid locomotion while retaining biological plausibility and robust performance at once remains an open question. We study this problem by proposing a biologically inspired spiking network, trained by different learning schemes and tested on the H1-2 Unitree Humanoid. items.title: Double determinants of quaternion matrices in the P-generalized determinant framework with applications
items.summary: Building on the P-generalized determinant over quaternions, we introduce the double determinant of arbitrary square quaternion matrices. We then apply the double determinant to obtain a determinant representation for the inverse of any invertible quaternion matrix, without the Hermitian restriction. items.summary: The European Union's Artificial Intelligence Act (AI Act) entered into force in August 2024, and its obligations apply in stages. Obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models have applied since August 2025, and transparency rules since August 2026. These obligations affect developers who share and deploy models and applications on public platforms such as Hugging Face (HF), the largest platform for distributing AI artifacts. However, little is known about how practitioners respond to the regulation in practice. To address this gap, we conducted an empirical study of explicit references to the AI Act on HF. items.summary: Reasoning models provide strong multimodal task understanding but struggle with sub-second control because deliberation increases decision latency. Fast decision models can meet the response window, yet prompting and few-shot examples do not readily provide the fine-grained experience required by a new task. items.summary: Biomolecular condensates exhibit surprisingly low surface tensions, despite forming dense, liquid-like phases. items.title: Does It Depend on the Split? Frozen Satellite Features vs. Fine-Tuned CNNs for Tree Species Mapping
items.summary: Self-supervised foundation models are often said to need fewer labels than supervised training. items.title: The Price of an Explanation: What Demanding Verifiable Artifacts Costs, and What It Buys Back
items.summary: Generative models produce many candidate solutions but provide no intrinsic signal by which to rank them. One mitigation is to demand a \emph{verifiable artifact}: a program that can be executed against the available evidence. items.title: Explainable AI for Solar PV Power Forecasting: From Model Selection to Trustworthy, Reproducible Deployment
items.summary: Machine learning (ML) is now a standard tool for forecasting the output of solar photovoltaic (PV) plants, yet published accuracy figures are often hard to compare and harder to trust. Many studies validate with random splits, report no reference forecast, and present feature attributions without saying what they can and cannot show. This paper reviews the main families of ML methods for PV power forecasting and resource assessment, from tree ensembles to deep and foundation models, and sets out a reproducible workflow that combines automated model search with explainable AI. items.title: ECHO: In-Context Behavior foundation model for Humanoid Whole-Body Control
items.summary: Humanoid behavior foundation models (BFMs) acquire diverse skills through large-scale motion imitation and massively parallel reinforcement learning, yet broad behavioral capability does not ensure precise execution across physical conditions. items.summary: Longitudinal PSMA-PET/CT registration is a key step in assessing treatment response in prostate cancer, and it requires more than generic alignment accuracy: the deformation must preserve lesion volume, so that measured changes in metabolic tumor volume (MTV) and total lesion glycolysis (TLG) reflect treatment response rather than registration artifacts. items.title: MatVerse: A Foundation Model for Materials Science
items.summary: Materials science involves highly heterogeneous scientific information, including textual knowledge, molecular and crystal structures, experimental characterization data, microscopy images, and structure-property relationships. We benchmark 9 histology FMs and 6 general-purpose models across four patch-level and two whole-slide image (WSI) datasets. We find that $D_4$ TTA remains a reliable post hoc improvement, but benefits diminish from $+1.98$ percentage points (pp)…

items.title: Severe but Harmless: Stress-Testing Shift Severity for Frozen Time-Series Forecasters
items.summary: Zero-shot time-series foundation models (TSFMs) have become attractive alternatives to task-specific models because they handle diverse downstream tasks, including anomaly detection and forecasting, without per-series training. However, time-series data undergo distribution shifts, and the dissimilarity between two regimes is commonly scored with statistical measures such as Wasserstein-1, where a higher score is read as a more severe shift. In systematic experiments using three established severity measures on nine regime shifts from three standard traffic datasets, we show that these measures do not reliably predict degradation for instance-normalized TSFMs. The regimes rated most severe…

items.title: On the Asymptotic Expansion of Massive Fields in Spherically Symmetric Systems
items.summary: The behavior of massive real scalar fields, when sourced by a central object, is usually assumed to follow a Yukawa falloff towards radial infinity. In this paper, we show that this is generically not the case, even for minimally coupled fields. Further, while the point-particle action provides a coordinate-invariant definition of the central object's scalar charge, we show that the coefficient one usually extracts at asymptotically large radii in the case of massive scalar fields is neither coordinate invariant nor identical to the scalar charge appearing in the point-particle action. We resolve this issue perturbatively by constructing matched asymptotic expansions and investigate the…

items.title: FM-Recon: Exploring Foundation Model Features for Accelerated Cardiac Cine MRI Reconstruction
items.summary: Foundation models have demonstrated strong feature extraction capabilities across various medical imaging tasks, yet their potential for MRI reconstruction remains largely unexplored, particularly within unrolled reconstruction networks and under artifact-corrupted inputs. In this work, we explore whether and how features from pretrained foundation models can benefit accelerated cardiac cine MRI reconstruction. To this end, we propose FM-Recon, a framework that refines and integrates extracted features from frozen image encoder of foundation models into an unrolled reconstruction network. Through extensive experiments on the CMRxRecon2023 dataset, we systematically evaluate foundation…

items.title: Open-fMIND: A Large-Scale Open-Access fMRI Corpus for Pretraining Brain Foundation Models
items.summary: Self-supervised pretraining has transformed language and vision, but its application to functional MRI (fMRI) is constrained by data access. The largest standardized fMRI resources are governed by data use agreements and dominated by a small number of acquisition protocols, while the thousands of openly licensed datasets on OpenNeuro are individually small, heterogeneously organized, and unprocessed. We present the first release of Open-fMIND, a uniformly preprocessed, openly accessible corpus of parcellated fMRI timeseries from 322 OpenNeuro studies, comprising 11,379 subjects and 45,731 functional runs. Each run is preprocessed with fMRIPrep and parcellated under 52 atlases spanning 14…

items.title: From Repositories to Training Environments: Scaling Long-Horizon Coding Agents with Environment Evolution Loop
items.summary: Training coding agents for long-horizon tasks requires environments with verifiable feedback. Existing pipelines often follow a linear process that ends with validation, establishing usability but providing little guidance on improving training value. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) often requires model rollouts or model training followed by downstream evaluation, with costs and feedback delays amplified on long-horizon tasks. How can we use timely, reliable proxy signals to improve training value and synthesize environments at scale? We present RepoFactory, an automated pipeline that converts real repositories into verifiable environments where agents build complete projects from scratch…

items.title: Entropy of Noncommutative Spaces
items.summary: We give an overview of the second quantisation of spectral triples and compute the entropy of the noncommutative space described by it in terms of a spectral action. This reviews earlier work by Chamseddine, Connes and the second author, but presented here concisely, including the procedure of second quantisation using infinite-dimensional Clifford algebras. We exemplify the theory by considering noncommutative metric spaces consisting of $N$ points. The entropy of these discrete spaces is explicitly computed, and we study the resulting entropic force as well as the evolution of the spaces in time.

items.title: Scribble Once, Segment the Sequence: Bidirectional Temporal Consistency for Weakly Supervised Segmentation in Echocardiography Sequences
items.summary: Temporal medical image segmentation relies on pixel-wise annotations, which are prohibitively expensive for long image sequences. Existing weakly-supervised methods reduce the annotation burden per frame but still require repeated annotations across the sequence. Furthermore, sparse supervision can result in temporally unstable representations. Addressing both challenges requires a model that can leverage strong spatial priors from large-scale pretraining while minimizing reliance on dense annotations. Frozen 2D vision foundation models provide a promising basis for this by offering transferable spatial representations with low trainable parameters. However, their lack of explicit temporal…

items.title: Region-VAD: Video Anomaly Localization and Detection via Region Selection
items.summary: Anomalies are local events, yet weakly supervised video anomaly detection scores them globally. Most methods pool an entire frame into a single vector, rank frames by that vector, and derive a location afterwards as a saliency map of the score. Full-frame pooling mixes the anomaly with its background, so a detector can reach competitive benchmark scores from scene context without being able to show where in the scene the anomaly occurs. We introduce Region-VAD, which first selects a region and then detects the anomaly from that region alone. Region-VAD selects an explicit rectangle over the tokens of a frozen foundation model and scores anomalousness only from the tokens inside the box,…

items.title: Evaluation-Free Recursive Self-Improvement for Coding Agents
items.summary: Recent self-improving coding agents have achieved strong benchmark performance by iteratively modifying their own executable implementations. A common pattern uses downstream task-derived evidence to decide which candidates or lineages continue evolving, which we term evaluate-and-select. Obtaining this signal requires repeatedly executing evolved agents on downstream tasks, so broader exploration incurs increasing evaluation cost, while repeated optimization against a fixed evaluation distribution may encourage benchmark-specific adaptation. We ask: can coding agents self-improve without downstream task evaluation inside the evolution loop? We introduce Explore-then-Integrate (ELITE),…

items.title: Calpha: Toward Native Biomolecular Intelligence in a General-Purpose Language Model
items.summary: Biomolecular foundation models predict the structures of proteins and their complexes accurately, and large language models (LLMs) reason in natural language, but the two remain separate: the abilities of the former are not part of a general-purpose LLM, and the reasoning of the latter does not enter a structure prediction. Calpha aims at one general model that folds proteins and complexes, understands protein sequence and structure, and lets its language reasoning influence the structures it predicts. This report covers the first step, in which an LLM outputs single-chain protein structures. Qwen3.5-9B reads a sequence enriched with ESM2 residue features. It can respond in text or emit a…

items.title: Interpretable deep concepts of organoid morphology
items.summary: Image-based classification of organoid morphologies can indicate drug response, viability, or successful differentiation. In recent work, learned representations outperform handcrafted features as the basis for downstream classifiers. However, their black-box nature hides the morphological cues a classifier relies on. Based on the foundation models DINOv3 (general-purpose) and ViTAMIn-O (organoid-specific), we train sparse autoencoders (SAEs) to learn interpretable concepts related to distinct organoid morphologies. We annotate concepts with spatial labels (organoid, organoid wall, background) and compute their dataset specificity and task relevance across five tasks. The spatial labels of…

items.title: A Recursive Construction of Perfect Arrays of Every Shape $2^{a_1}\times\cdots\times2^{a_d}$ over the Unit Quaternions
items.summary: We extend the recursive construction of perfect and odd perfect sequences over the simple unit quaternions $\Qe=\{\pm1,\pm i,\pm j,\pm k\}$ of Blake to arrays of any dimension. The three operations of that construction act on one direction of an array at a time, and are valid whenever the array is periodic in the remaining directions. Starting from a perfect array $P$ of shape $M_2\times\cdots\times M_d$ they give perfect arrays of shape $2^a\times M_2\times\cdots\times M_d$ for every $a\ge0$, with explicit index functions and with the array orthogonality property for the divisor $2$ in the lifted direction; from $a=5$ on these arrays are, in general, Kronecker products of a sequence with…

items.title: VA-Assembly: View-Aligned Score Guidance for Training-Free 3D Part Assembly
items.summary: Image-to-3D foundation models have improved 3D reconstruction, but typically produce monolithic representations without explicit part-level structure. Part-aware generation and learning-based assembly methods often require part-level supervision, category-specific priors, or paired part-layout training data. We instead consider a practical but underexplored setting in which independently prepared or generated 3D parts have no predefined inter-part relationships, shared coordinate frames, or consistent scales, and must be assembled into a reference-consistent object from a single image. We present VA-Assembly, a training-free framework for 3D part assembly through part-level transformation…

items.title: A Seismic Foundation Model for Dense Feature Extraction
items.summary: Deep-learning-based seismic interpretation is constrained by scarce high-quality annotations, and most existing models are trained separately for individual tasks. We present SeisDFE, a 7B-parameter seismic foundation model for dense feature extraction, pretrained on 5.34 million 2D images derived from more than 500 seismic volumes. A three-stage pretraining strategy, combining discriminative self-supervised learning, Gram feature anchoring, and multi-resolution adaptation, improves feature discriminability while preserving spatial coherence. With its encoder frozen, SeisDFE supports seismic facies classification, salt detection, fault detection, and relative geologic time estimation. It…

items.title: Robotic Reward Models in the Foundation-Model Era
items.summary: Robotic reward models (RRMs) use foundation models to replace per-task reward engineering with reusable, task-conditioned evaluation. Yet under one name, their outputs answer different questions, from whether a task succeeded to which execution is better. This survey organizes 114 methods into five semantic families by the question their native outputs answer: Outcome, Absolute Progress, Relative, Temporal Value, and Hybrid. Within this taxonomy, we review how model design determines what an evaluator can judge, how raw experience becomes supervision, and how existing evaluation practice tests the result. The review exposes a gap: agreement with demonstration order and downstream policy…

items.title: A note on Padmanabhan's path-integral duality
items.summary: We develop a field-theoretic implementation of Padmanabhan's principle of invariance under the duality $\mathcal S \rightarrow {L_0^2}/{\mathcal S}$, where ${\mathcal S}$ is the proper length (the action integral along a particle's trajectory) and $L_0$ is a quantum of length. Starting from the particle propagator and its Schwinger proper-time representation, we derive the wave operator associated with the duality transformation in terms of a scalar field, rather than a point particle. The resulting theory is governed by a nonlocal operator involving modified Bessel functions. items.title: Boson Stars with Ayón--Beato--García nonlinear electrodynamics
items.summary: In this paper, we study spherically symmetric boson star solutions in Einstein gravity minimally coupled to Ayón--Beato--García nonlinear electrodynamics and a massive complex scalar field. We find that these solutions exist only when the electric charge $q$ is below a critical value. Within this range, solutions with relatively small charges can exhibit a gravitational blueshift, and the radial mass function becomes negative in some regions while the ADM mass remains positive. For larger charges, frozen boson-star solutions emerge as the scalar-field frequency $ω$ approaches zero. items.title: Progressive Layer-wise Supervision: Deep-to-Shallow Supervision Annealing for Efficient and Robust Speech Deepfake Detection
items.summary: Speech foundation models pretrained via self-supervised learning provide powerful representations for deepfake detection, yet we find that standard fine-tuning exploits only the deepest transformer layers-leaving the majority of the network's capacity discriminatively inert. Layer-wise probing of XLS-R-128 reveals that the top two-thirds of the transformer stack contribute negligibly to anti-spoofing performance after standard fine-tuning, a phenomenon we term shallow-layer dormancy. We connect this observation to the representational redundancy of pretrained transformers: adjacent layers encode highly similar information, and fine-tuning without explicit intermediate supervision…

items.title: SCoRe: Support-Calibrated Role Fusion for Training-Free Cross-Domain Few-Shot Segmentation
items.summary: We present SCoRe (Support-Calibrated Role fusion), a framework to utilize two complementary vision foundation model-based (VFM) segmenters for training-free cross-domain few-shot segmentation (CD-FSS). Our approach is based on the observation that current VFMs for CD-FSS possess capabilities where one model locates the correct object, while another model computes the better contour. Our approach uses: 1. a method to identify a VFM segmenter to lead Few-Shot Segmentation (FSS) task for a given concept, 2. a novel deterministic boundary correction method using bands of near- and far-pixels at the lead segmenter's predicted boundary of an object, and 3. a region correction mechanism for the…

items.title: Harmonic branches of Einstein--ModMax--scalar field gravity: exact solutions and regularity II
items.summary: We integrate harmonic solution branches of Einstein--ModMax--Scalar field gravity, keeping the electromagnetic phase \(\tanΘ=\mathcal{G}/\mathcal{F}\) non-constant. For each family we first solve the field equations $(a(\s),b(\s),c(\s))$ and reconstruct the physical functions $f,ω,k,A_t,A_\varphi,φ$. In the same section we then select the Schwarzschild or Coulomb harmonic function, impose the regular horizon conditions, identify the ModMax solution, and state its Maxwell limit. Two theorems distinguish a constant electromagnetic phase from an exact static charge rescaling and show how twist prevents constant diagonal rescalings of the electromagnetic potentials at fixed metric and scalar.…

items.title: Local Spike Timing Enables Gradient-based Learning in Neural Microcircuits
items.summary: arXiv:2609.08070v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The brain uses discrete spikes for dynamic computation, yet in the fields of computational neuroscience and brain-inspired computing, how neural microcircuits (NMCs) solve temporal credit assignment using local spike timing remains a fundamental open question. Dominant spiking neural network (SNN) approaches circumvent this by approximating backpropagation through surrogate gradients, decoupling learning from biological spike timing. items.title: Lightweight Semantic EEG Foundation Model for Frozen Cross-Disorder Transfer
items.summary: arXiv:2610.05503v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large-scale EEG foundation models have demonstrated promising transferability across neurological disorders, but often require millions of parameters and substantial computational resources. In this paper, we present the Universal Semantic EEG Foundation Model (USE-FM), a lightweight EEG foundation model that learns transferable neural representations through self-supervised signal reconstruction on the Temple University Hospital EEG Corpus (TUEG). After pretraining, the encoder is frozen and evaluated on two clinically distinct downstream tasks, abnormal EEG detection (TUAB) and epileptic seizure recognition (TUEP), using a unified…

items.title: Similar Predictive Fit but Different Latent Dynamics: Characterizing Learned Dynamical Structure in Personalized Models of Brain Disorders
items.summary: arXiv:2610.10850v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: As AI models move toward clinical decision-making and personalized treatment, understanding \emph{what} a model learns is important beyond predictive accuracy alone. We investigate whether personalized latent dynamics reveal clinically associated differences even when predictive fit is similar. A lightweight CNN--Transformer EEG foundation model pretrained on the Temple University EEG Corpus (TUEG) extracts segment-level representations. Using the Temple University Epilepsy Corpus (TUEP), representations are mapped to a shared latent-state space, and sparse multinomial logistic transition distributions (mLTD) are fit independently…

items.title: Efficient Poincar\'e Convolutions through Patch-Statistics Factorization
items.summary: arXiv:2611.18125v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Published implementations of the Poincar\'e convolution in Hyperbolic Neural Networks++ (HNN++) map every overlapping image patch to the Poincar\'e ball before evaluating its score. We show that the clipped score depends on each patch only through two statistics, its squared norm and its inner products with the filters, which a native convolution and a single-channel box filter compute directly. items.title: Ternary Spiking Neural Networks Enhanced by Complemented Neurons and Membrane Potential Aggregation
items.summary: arXiv:2601.15598v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) are promising energy-efficient models and powerful framworks of modeling neuron dynamics. However, existing binary spiking neurons exhibit limited biological plausibilities and low information capacity. Recently developed ternary spiking neuron possesses higher consistency with biological principles (i.e. excitation-inhibition balance mechanism). Despite of this, the ternary spiking neuron suffers from defects including iterative information loss, temporal gradient vanishing and irregular distributions of membrane potentials. To address these issues, we propose Complemented Ternary Spiking Neuron (CTSN), a…

items.title: Lift, See, Act: Hierarchical Robot Policy Pretraining with 3D Foundation Models
items.summary: Robot policy pretraining based on human videos is crucial for improving the policy's generalization ability. One main challenge for this task is the lack of explicit action-relevant representations in such unlabeled data. Recent works tend to estimate 3D hand motion trajectories from videos using 3D foundation models (3D FMs). However, they keep solely the sparse trajectories as supervision, ignoring the rich, fine-grained information produced during the trajectory extraction process. To address this issue, we propose LSA, a hierarchical robot policy pretraining framework that includes three phases: Lift, See, and Act. items.title: Tabular Foundation Models as Emulators for Forecasting Terrestrial Ecosystem Dynamics
items.summary: Process-based terrestrial biosphere models such as the Ecosystem Demography (ED) model underpin global carbon budgets, but their cost limits global, high-resolution and scenario-rich simulation. Deep emulators such as DeepED reduce that cost but require task-specific architectures and training. Tabular foundation models offer a different route: TabPFN predicts new rows by in-context learning, without being trained on the task. We compare TabPFN-3.5 with two DeepED baselines, $DeepED_{LSTM}$ and $DeepED_{Transformer}$, on CarbonGlobe's overall evaluation, which trains on a uniform 1/16 sample of sites and tests on the other 50,779, predicting the 40-year state of all seven ED outputs. items.title: AdaModalX: Synchronization-Free MFM Inference for Distributed Multimodal Mobile Sensing via Progressive Data Orchestration
items.summary: Multimodal foundation models (MFMs) support generalizable inference in distributed mobile sensing applications by integrating heterogeneous data streams. However, existing MFM inference pipelines typically require complete and synchronized multimodal inputs, whereas mobile sensing streams arrive asynchronously due to network variability and heterogeneous data volumes across modalities. Waiting for all modalities increases end-to-end latency, while inference with incomplete inputs can reduce accuracy. We argue that multimodal inference should depend on the utility of available information rather than modality completeness. Based on this principle, we propose AdaModalX, a progressive…

items.title: Taint Analysis via Heap-Aware Propagation
items.summary: Taint analysis for C depends on how precisely the analysis tracks tainted values as they flow through memory objects. Without field sensitivity, a tainted object field can spuriously taint an entire object, producing significant false alarms. In this paper, we present a field-sensitive taint analysis that combines Data Structure Analysis (DSA) for field-sensitive points-to information with a data-flow analysis for tracking explicit dependencies. We identify that existing DSA-style analyses lose precision on a common object pattern: a C struct object that mixes scalar fields with a flexible array member. items.title: TrainExplorer: Autonomous LLM Post-Training via Plan-and-Decouple Exploration
items.summary: LLM-based agents can automate model post-training, accelerating progress toward recursive self-improvement. Despite their promise, existing approaches remain under-explored and face two main challenges: (1) strategy lock-in that limits exploration beyond the initial strategy; and (2) coupled execution that obscures the effects of individual modifications. To address these challanges, we propose TrainExplorer, a multi-agent framework for autonomous post-training, that incorporates strategy planning and execution decoupling, to achieve broaden strategy exploration. First, strategy planning draws on scientific literature to construct a candidate search space of training strategies. Then,…

items.title: FiuMD: Heterogeneous Batching for Coarse-Grained Molecular Dynamics with Neural Network Potentials
items.summary: FiuMD is a GPU molecular dynamics engine that advances many independent biomolecular simulations as a single batch, even when the systems differ in size, topology, force-field parameters, periodic box, timestep, or thermostat parameters. FiuMD started as a fork of TorchMD and reworks its system representation, force evaluation, and integration to handle such heterogeneous batches. items.title: Stimulus-Driven Reconfigurable Memristors with Volatile-to-Nonvolatile Transition for Spatiotemporal Neuromorphic Computing.

items.title: FMint-SDE: A Multimodal Foundation Model for Accelerating Numerical Simulation of SDEs via Error Correction
items.summary: Abstract. Fast and accurate simulation of dynamical systems is a fundamental challenge across scientific and engineering domains. items.title: Is the Bitter Lesson coming to genomic prediction? An untuned tabular foundation model matches or beats specialized methods
items.summary: Genomic prediction (GP) is dominated by models designed around assumptions about how genetic variation affects phenotypes. Here we asked how well a general-purpose pretrained tabular foundation model called TabPFN-3.5 does with no genetics-specific modeling and no tuning when given marker genotypes directly. We benchmarked TabPFN-3.5 using a published comparison of 18 GP methods on 18 traits in six plant species. Against the published means, TabPFN-3.5 ranked first on 11 of 18 traits and had the best median rank. Because the published benchmark did not identify its test sets, we reran GBLUP, RKHS and elastic-net models on the same splits as TabPFN-3.5. Against the best of these, TabPFN-3.5…

items.title: From quantum brain to quantum mind: The ontological promotion gap in quantum-biological theories of consciousness.
items.summary: Quantum effects in biological systems are increasingly investigated at molecular, cellular, and neural scales, yet evidence for quantum organization in a living brain does not by itself determine the ontological status of the conscious states realized by that brain. This article distinguishes seven claims often compressed under "quantum consciousness": quantum occurrence, causal relevance, constitutive relevance, phenomenal bridging, phenomenal individuation, quantum mental status, and quantum-formal adequacy. items.summary: Atomistic foundation models have emerged as a promising route to DFT-level accuracy for materials simulation with complex chemical environments. However, their reliability across competing bonding regimes and, more importantly, how complex bonding affects predictions of material properties remain unclear. Among materials with competing bonding regimes, sodium storage in hard carbon poses a substantial challenge. items.title: Gravitational Corrections to OPE Coefficients
items.summary: The short-distance singular behavior of correlation functions of quantum field theories in curved spacetime is a universal property shared by all well-behaved states (known as Hadamard states). For two-point functions this takes the form of the Hadamard tail of free scalars and its generalizations to spinning fields and interacting theories. In this work, we compute similar universal curvature corrections to curved-space OPE coefficients in a short-distance expansion for interacting quantum field theories in general dimensions. Its end-to-end architecture combines perception, memory management, and multi-step reasoning. A shared training and deployment pipeline supports interaction with both conventional 2D graphical interfaces and complex 3D simulated worlds. We first continue pre-training on a dataset constructed from tens of thousands of hours of device-level keyboard and mouse interaction. items.summary: The release of GPT-6 Astra marks the emergence of a new paradigm in robotics: agentic robotics. Within weeks, frontier models with agentic harnesses matched or exceeded task-specific policies on many embodied benchmarks. Instead of training a dedicated policy for each family of tasks, an agentic robotic system applies a foundation model to open-world embodied tasks. It operates in a closed loop: observing the environment, interpreting user intent, reasoning about the task, invoking skills and tools, verifying outcomes, and adapting its strategy. items.summary: Web platforms record user and item activity in relational databases whose schemas differ from platform to platform, which makes it difficult to transfer predictive models between them. Relational foundation models address this through cross-database pretraining, yet recent improvements have relied on increasingly large pretraining corpora. items.summary: Spatio-temporal foundation models (STFMs) require large-scale training corpora, yet synchronized observations and spatial metadata are costly to acquire and curate, limiting the availability of suitable data. By contrast, time-series data are abundant and easier to collect. Since observations at each location form a time series, this motivates a natural question: can abundant time-series data enhance STFMs when spatio-temporal observations are scarce? To bridge this gap, we propose T2ST, a data-efficient training framework that augments limited spatio-temporal observations with selected auxiliary time series and transfers knowledge from a frozen time-series foundation model. items.summary: Foundation models produce high-dimensional latent representations in which suitably designed statistical decision rules can be effective yet analytically tractable. We study such detectors in the high-dimensional regime, where latent dimension and training sample size grow proportionally. items.summary: Published implementations of the Poincaré convolution in Hyperbolic Neural Networks++ (HNN++) map every overlapping image patch to the Poincaré ball before evaluating its score. items.title: SWIFT: Sample-Wise Instance Fine-Tuning of Time-Series Foundation Models for Forecasting
items.summary: While current few-shot adaptation strategies for time series forecasting foundation models are predominantly dataset-centric, the necessity of obtaining an additional dataset for the finetuning process poses a significant hurdle for adoption. To address this constraint, we propose Sample-Wise Instance Fine-Tuning (SWIFT), a novel forecasting adaptation framework that achieves fine-grained specialization by leveraging structural priors from the target instance's own history. items.title: FlexCast: Flexible Context Learning for Time Series Foundation Models
items.summary: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) based on autoregressive (AR) next-token prediction entangle two factors: variable-context conditioning and prediction-unit factorization with autoregressive rollout. items.summary: We derive an exact dynamical consistency relation for a smooth, periodically compactified five-dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet cosmology sourced by a real, minimally coupled canonical scalar field. For a spatially flat Friedmann--Lemaitre--Robertson--Walker slicing and a generally time-dependent warp factor, a contraction of the bulk equations eliminates both the scalar potential and the bulk cosmological constant. A direct orthonormal-curvature reconstruction gives the independent diagonal and mixed field equations and verifies the contracted Gauss--Bonnet identity. The integrated relation separates an exact total derivative from the dynamically active Lovelock sector. Importantly,…

items.title: Foundation Tensor Networks Generalize Across Quantum Lattice Systems
items.summary: Neural quantum states and tensor networks have emerged as leading techniques for simulating quantum many-body systems. However, disordered systems remain extremely challenging in both frameworks as they require computation of the ground state for every realization of the disorder. Recently, neural quantum states have been used to construct foundation models that generate the ground state directly from the Hamiltonian. Still, they are hindered by the need to perform extensive sampling to estimate observables. To address these difficulties, we introduce the foundation tensor network (FTN), which uses a neural network to generate the tensor network representation of the ground-state…

items.title: On the Utility of Pre-Trained Visual Representations for Policy Learning of Contact-Rich Insertion Tasks
items.summary: Visuomotor imitation learning has become a predominant paradigm for real-world robotic manipulation, yet it remains data-inefficient and brittle to task-irrelevant visual shifts. Pre-trained visual representations promise to ease this burden by distilling priors from internet-scale data, but the ``right'' representation for robotics remains unresolved: existing studies span broad but sparse task distributions and reach conclusions that vary and even conflict, pointing to strong task and setting dependence. We examine this question by bringing a magnifying glass to a common contact-rich manipulation task: insertion. We compare representations from widely used vision foundation models…

items.title: FROM MATHEMATICAL SUPERINTELLIGENCE TO PHYSICAL DISCOVERY
items.summary: Recent advances in artificial intelligence suggest that coordinated populations of capablereasoning agents may solve mathematical problems of extraordinary complexity. Suchachievements raise a distinct question: Can comparable systems advance fundamental physicsby identifying the physical mechanisms responsible for nature’s observed behavior, rather thanmerely extending mathematical descriptions already accepted by scientific convention?This paper proposes a human-directed, observation-first AI research architecture forinvestigating Space-Phase (SP3) theory. SP3 proposes that physical space is a participatingmedium interacting with energy through nested configurations, conditioning,…

items.title: SpaRRTa: A Synthetic Benchmark for Evaluating Spatial Intelligence in Visual Foundation Models
items.summary: Abstract Visual Foundation Models (VFMs), such as DINO and CLIP, excel in semantic understanding of images but exhibit limited spatial reasoning capabilities, which limits their applicability to embodied systems. As a result, recent work has incorporated some 3D tasks (such as depth estimation) into VFM training. However, VFM performance remains inconsistent across other spatial tasks, raising the question of whether these models truly possess spatial awareness or overfit to specific 3D objectives. To address this question, we introduce the Spatial Relation Recognition Task (SpaRRTa) benchmark, which evaluates the ability of VFMs to identify static directional relations between visible…

items.title: Laser-guided ion dynamics in a dual-mode memristor for bioinspired neuronal and synaptic integration
items.summary: Abstract Neuromorphic computing aims to replicate the parallel, adaptive nature of biological intelligence in electronic systems. Despite considerable advances in memristor technology, material-encoded neurosynaptic bifunctionality has not been demonstrated. We introduce a laser-guided dual-mode memristor that integrates both volatility for neuronal spiking and nonvolatility for synaptic plasticity within a single-phase material. By precisely modulating silver ion dynamics through XeCl excimer laser irradiation, we achieve local and dynamic control of the dual-mode memristive behavior without requiring a heterogeneous device array or stacking. The neurosynaptic tunability with optimal…

items.title: UVM: neuron verification
items.summary: The significant growth in Neuromorphic engineering in the last few years has generated a multitude of biologically plausible neuron models that have been developed into Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) and Application Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC) designs. These neuron models range in complexity, from the Integrate and Fire model to the Hodgkin-Huxley model. When creating fixed point implementations of these models, it is prudent to ensure the dynamic range of the fixed point conversion has been correctly chosen. However, verifying neuron model implementations in simulation requires a significant amount of time to achieve an acceptable coverage; that is, everything that could be…

items.title: Learning the spikes
items.summary: Existing AI methods consume vast amounts of power due to their large scale and intrinsic redundancy. Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer a biologically plausible alternative that enables systems that are of a low Size, Weight and Power (SWaP) profile, once implemented. However, there is limited commercial availability of Neuromorphic processors to efficiently implement these SNNs on chip, resulting in a requirement to develop FPGA-based Neuromorphic processing. The same can be said for Neuromorphic sensors, driving a trend to develop techniques for encoding existing sensor data into an event-based format for use with Neuromorphic processors. This paper presents a very efficient, low power…

items.title: Modelling dynamic systems transfer functions from events in computational neuromorphic imaging
items.summary: Event Vision Sensing (EVS) report threshold crossings of log-irradiance, so a static optical system imaging a static scene produces no output at all. The classical procedure for measuring a Point Spread Function (PSF), illuminating the system with a constant point source, therefore has no event-based equivalent: the probe must carry a temporal profile, and that profile becomes part of the measurement. A growing body of Computational Neuromorphic Imaging (CNI) work already exploits this, pairing engineered or modulated optics with event sensing, but each system adopts a particular excitation together with a particular reading of the event stream without the correspondence between the two…

items.title: Candidate alternative splice-junction architecture at a Ganoderma carnitine acetyltransferase-like locus: an accession-traceable RNA-seq reanalysis
items.summary: Abstract A focused reanalysis of public Ganoderma transcriptomic resources evaluated two candidate splice-junction paths (A and B) at a putative carnitine acetyltransferase-like locus (MSTRG.5584). Forty RNA-seq run labels from five genomic backgrounds were reconciled with accession metadata and examined using targeted splice-spanning read counts; 11 undercovered libraries underwent complete read-1 recounting. Both candidate junction paths were observed in all five backgrounds. In libraries with any focal read support, mean junction-A fractions were descriptively greater in mycelium-labeled than in fruiting-body-labeled groups, with background-level differences ranging from +0.190 to…

items.title: Infrared Life: Coherent Josephson Radiation in Microtubule Networks, Radiometric Signatures, and Quantum Synchronization in Living Systems
items.summary: This paper investigates non-thermal electromagnetic radiation generated within livingorganisms. In addition to universal blackbody radiation dominating the infrared spectrum,living systems generate narrow-band, coherent infrared radiation aligned with the 8–13 µmtransparency window of Earth’s atmosphere. This emission avoids complete thermalization,acts independently of classical thermal radiance, and represents an evolutionary hallmarkof biological order. The radiation is shown to originate within multi-connected networks ofsuperconducting microtubules functioning as Josephson junctions during action potentialpropagation. We present radiometric measurements on porcine brain tissue slices…

items.title: GenAI-enabled accounting information systems competence: Antecedents, perceived usefulness, AI ethics awareness, and career readiness outcomes.
items.summary: This study examines GenAI-enabled accounting information systems competence (GAISC) among accounting and auditing students and its relationships with GenAI readiness (GAR), perceived ease of use (PEOU), digital learning self-efficacy (DLSE), facilitating conditions (FC), perceived usefulness (PU), AI ethics awareness (AIEA), and career readiness (CR). The model is anchored in Socio-Technical Systems Theory (STS) and Social Cognitive Career Theory (SCCT), with technology readiness, TAM, self-efficacy, and facilitating-condition logic used as construct-level underpinning mechanisms. Survey data from 471 students at five Vietnamese universities were analyzed using PLS-SEM, complemented by a…

items.title: In silico drug discovery framework leveraging biomedical foundation models and evaluating generative models-a use case on 3CL pro .
items.summary: AI models such as foundation models and generative models have shown promise for aiding drug discovery alongside traditional cheminformatics and bioinformatics tools and physics-based approaches. In this study, we design a workflow that integrates these AI methods to generate molecules alongside established informatic and predictive filtering approaches to streamline downselection of molecules from the massive and noisy result sets generated by AI. This workflow evaluates generative methods based on validity, reliability, diversity, similarity, hallucination and campaign needs. Analyses are made on the original proprietary dataset to determine molecular property thresholds for screening…

items.title: MicroDUET: a dual-headed genomic foundation model for pathogen surveillance
items.summary: Pathogen genomic surveillance works from raw reads, assembled genomes and alignments, representations that are slow and costly to compare at scale. Compact embeddings from genomic language models offer an alternative, but surveillance requires resolving both evolutionary ancestry (phylogeny) and phenotypic capability (function) - which need not co-vary. Here we present MicroDUET, which adapts a 26.6-million-parameter ProkBERT backbone with two 3.5-million-parameter adapter heads: a phylogeny head trained contrastively on genome windows from the same microbes, and a function head trained to identify genes across taxa. On held-out retrieval benchmarks, the phylogeny head returned the correct…

items.title: Systematic benchmarking of molecular foundation models for natural-product annotation and biosynthetic inference
items.summary: Abstract Molecular foundation models offer a potential route to improve natural-product annotation and support biosynthetic inference, but their utility across these tasks remains insufficiently characterized. We benchmarked eight foundation-model representations against Morgan fingerprints across five tasks covering natural-product-likeness, natural product chemical class prediction, PMN and KEGG pathway association, and PlantCyc reaction-neighbor prediction. Models were evaluated under random and scaffold-based splits using both full data and sample-efficiency settings. In the full data setting, MolFormer achieved the highest mean AUROC for natural product likeness prediction, while…

items.title: LUNA-FM: a subword foundation model for long non-coding RNAs for functional inference.
items.summary: RNA foundation models (FMs) have shown promise for RNA identification and functional annotation. However, many use single-nucleotide tokenization, which produces long input sequences and can increase computational costs when modelling long RNAs, including long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs). To address these limitations, we introduce LUNA-FM ( Length-efficient s U bword-based N ucleic A cid F oundation M odel) , an RNA language model pretrained on approximately 28 million redundancy-filtered ncRNA sequences. LUNA-FM combines subword tokenization with a long context transformer, enabling efficient modelling of long RNA transcripts. We systematically evaluate tokenization strategies and…

items.title: Understanding plant UPR from structural and comparative perspectives.
items.summary: The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is central to protein, lipid, Ca2+, and redox homeostasis. ER stress occurs when oxidative protein-folding capacity is exceeded or lipid composition becomes abnormal. To restore ER and cellular homeostasis, the cell initiates the unfolded protein response (UPR)-a transcriptional response that amplifies the ER's capacity for protein folding, degradation, and lipid biosynthesis. Our understanding of plant UPR activation mechanisms remains limited compared with yeast and mammalian systems. Here, we compare the structural composition of the plant UPR sensors, inositol-requiring enzyme 1 and basic-region leucine zipper 28, with their yeast and animal homologs;…

items.title: Toward precision nanomedicine via artificial intelligence guided design and prediction.
items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is advancing nanomedicine development by linking formulation variables and biological context with delivery, therapeutic efficacy, and safety. This review examines AI assisted formulation design, centralized formulation databases, prediction of nanoparticle self assembly, and models of cell and tissue selective delivery, biodistribution, and therapeutic outcomes. Recent advances in predicting nanotoxicity and nanoparticle induced immune responses further emphasize the importance of incorporating safety endpoints into nanomedicine optimization. Beyond nanocarrier engineering, foundation models and multimodal analyses of single-cell and spatial data are expanding…

items.title: Fluid eMTBR-tau243 as a Biomarker of Mixed 3-Repeat and 4-Repeat Tau Pathology.
items.summary: Importance Neurodegenerative diseases with abnormal tau protein aggregation in the brain (ie, tauopathies) can be classified by the tau isoform that accumulates: 3-repeat (3R), 4-repeat (4R), or mixed 3R/4R tauopathies, which include chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), some forms of frontotemporal lobar degeneration, and Alzheimer disease (AD). The endogenously cleaved form of tau microtubule binding region containing the residue 243 (eMTBR-tau243) can be detected in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and blood and has been associated with AD tau pathology, but its specificity and biological interpretation in non-AD tauopathies remains unclear. Objective To evaluate biofluid eMTBR-tau243 in a…

items.title: HDAC6 Inhibition Promotes Peripheral Nerve Development and Regeneration via Neurofilament Acetylation.
items.summary: Peripheral nerve injury remains challenging due to limited neuronal regeneration. Histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6) regulates microtubule dynamics, but its role in peripheral nervous system (PNS) development and repair is incompletely understood. This study investigates the expression, function, and mechanism of HDAC6 in PNS maturation and regeneration. HDAC6 was abundantly expressed in dorsal root ganglia and sciatic nerves. During postnatal development (P1-P28), HDAC6 expression progressively declined, inversely correlating with increased α-tubulin K40 and global acetylation. Pharmacological HDAC6 inhibition with Tubastatin A (Tub A) or suberoylanilide hydroxamic acid (SAHA) accelerated…

items.title: NiCl 2 affect N- and O -alkylations during alkaloid biosynthesis in Penicillium oxalicum .
items.summary: Oxaline is one fungal alkaloid possessing important citotoxicity and inhibiting tubulin polymerisation. The alkaloids in this series are differentiated by the degree of alkylation promoted by SAM-dependent methyl transferases, being oxaline the end product in the biosynthetic cascade. During our studies, it was found that the addition of NiCl2 into liquid culture of P. oxalicum affect the distribution of these alkaloids, lowering the production of oxaline and enhancing the amount of methylglandicoline A and glandicoline C, two unreported natural products. Ni(II) addition also resulted in the production of a pair of E/Z isomers of N-formyl α,β-dehydro-DOPA, found only at trace amounts in…

items.title: Dual-Mode MoS 2 /PdSe 2 /WS 2 Van Der Waals Heterostructure for Self-Powered Polarization Sensing and Neuromorphic Processing.
items.summary: Harsh maritime environments demand compact visual devices capable of self-powered photodetection, polarization sensing, and motion-trajectory extraction for onboard processing. Here, we demonstrate a bias-switchable MoS 2 /PdSe 2 /WS 2 van der Waals heterostructure (vdWH) that integrates self-powered polarization-sensitive photodetection and optoelectronic synaptic functionality. At a drain-source voltage (V ds ) of 0 V, built-in electric fields efficiently separate photogenerated carriers, enabling self-powered broadband detection over the 405-658 nm spectral range. The device exhibits a maximum responsivity of 1345 mA W -1 , a specific detectivity of 8.89 × 10 10 Jones, and rapid…

items.title: Ion-Access Engineering for High-Performance Vertical Organic Electrolyte-Gated Transistors.
items.summary: Organic electrolyte-gated transistors (OEGTs) are promising platforms for bioelectronics and neuromorphic systems owing to their low-voltage operation and strong ionic-electronic coupling. However, in vertical OEGTs, which offer higher current densities and faster switching, the semiconductor channel is often shielded from direct electrolyte contact, limiting ionic accessibility and resulting in inefficient gate coupling and slow switching dynamics. Here, we introduce a photolithography-free ion-access strategy for vertical OEGTs, combining femtosecond laser micropatterning with inkjet-printed solid-state electrolytes. Laser-defined pores penetrating the top electrode and semiconductor…

items.title: Molecularly Programmed Stress Dissipation Strategy for Ultrastretchable Neuromorphic Electronics.
items.summary: Intrinsically stretchable organic synaptic transistors (ISOSTs) using semiconducting polymers (SPs) hold promise for on-body signal processing by mimicking biological synaptic functions and processing temporal bio-signals directly at or near the point of data acquisition. However, conventional SPs designed primarily to increase polymer softness and mechanical compliance often lack molecular-level mechanisms for effective stress dissipation, thereby limiting device-level stretchability to below 100% and causing substantial degradation in electrical performance. Here, we demonstrate ISOSTs achieving 150% device-level stretchability through molecularly programmed stress dissipation (MPSD) of…

items.title: Algorithmic bias in spike encoding schemes for SNN-based RF applications: an investigation
items.summary: Data-to-spike conversion using spike encoding schemes is one of the key stages in the development pipeline of Neuromorphic techniques for RF applications. However, many studies have not considered algorithmic bias in these encoding schemes at any stage of the development pipeline. For this, the paper assesses the impact of data-to-spike conversion in SNNs for RF applications through SNN-based parameter estimation. It was found that the use of encoded spike trains from different encoding schemes deteriorated the SNNs’ performance in the parameter estimation task, and the discriminatory behaviour of the encoding schemes on the selected RF atomic signals was observed through the…
