items.summary: We study which training and calibration data help three open models solve ARC-AGI-2 tasks when the solver runs offline on four L4 GPUs for at most 12 hours. items.title: Open-HumanScale: An Open Recipe for Scaling Human and Robot Experience for Embodied Foundation Models
items.summary: Egocentric human video offers a scalable source of manipulation priors for robot learning, yet translating raw data scale into generalizable robot policies demands rigorous data curation and training recipes. items.title: Transforming Integer Grids to Spatial Intuition: Perception, Not Planning, Governs ARC-AGI-3
items.summary: Sample-efficient fluid intelligence requires agents that rapidly form working models of unfamiliar interactive environments. items.summary: Coding agents powered by models such as GPT-6-Astra connect spatial reasoning with executable robot behavior, raising the question of how such agents can produce lasting improvements in robot capabilities from physical interaction. items.title: TailSteer: Trajectory-Tail Steering for Drift-Resistant Multi-turn Image Editing
items.summary: Strong single-turn editing performance does not guarantee reliable multi-turn interaction: as edited outputs are repeatedly reused, small unintended changes can accumulate into severe visual drift. items.title: Dexterous Robotic Hands in the Foundation-Model Era: A Full-Stack Survey of Hardware, Data, Cross-Embodiment Transfer, Learning, and Evaluation
items.summary: Dexterous robotic hands are increasingly coupled to large-scale human data and foundation models, yet progress in hardware, representation learning and evaluation is often assessed separately. items.title: Beyond the principle-practice gap: Responsible AI as situated epistemic and ethical practice
items.summary: Responsible AI scholarship has found that ethical principles are frequently not reflected in AI design and development. Conceptualised as a `gap' between principle and practice, this is framed as a problem of implementation, awareness or compliance, and by implication, a deficit of systems or individual behaviour. items.summary: Generalist robot policies are trained on static offline datasets, yet physical manipulation unfolds sequentially across stages. items.summary: We examine how the geometry of rotating black holes in linear, shift-symmetric Einstein--scalar--Gauss--Bonnet (EsGB) gravity changes the limiting tidal equilibria of white dwarfs (WDs). items.title: Interactive World Simulation with Cosmos for Physical AI
items.summary: We present a shared framework that adapts Cosmos world foundation models for real-time interactive world simulation in Physical AI. By streaming visual observations in response to actions and scene controls, the framework enables users and embodied agents to interact with evolving virtual environments. It supports both predicting the visual consequences of actions and generating observations from physical state maintained by an external simulator. items.title: Adapting Sleep Foundation Models for Dense Sleep Spindle Localization
items.summary: Adapting sleep foundation models to dense electroencephalography (EEG) event localization is challenging because multi-second representations may not preserve sufficient temporal detail for precise boundary recovery. items.summary: Dipolar boson stars consist of two scalar-field lumps held in static equilibrium by the balance between gravitational attraction and scalar repulsion. items.title: A 3D foundation model unifying CT interpretation and segmentation
items.summary: Radiologists interpret computed tomography (CT) scans by jointly determining what a finding represents and where it lies in three-dimensional (3D) anatomy. items.title: A Geometric No-Go Theorem for Regular Black Holes in Scalar-Tensor Theories
items.summary: Perturbative instabilities generically puzzles singularity-free spacetimes, including non-singular bounce, traversible wormholes and regular black holes (RBHs). items.title: Graph Foundation Models Can Become Effective Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detectors
items.summary: Multivariate time series anomaly detection (MTSAD) relies on modeling both temporal dynamics and inter-sensor dependencies to identify complex system faults. items.title: UniLoop: Unified Loop Closure Detection from Retrieval to Geometric Verification and Relative Pose Estimation
items.summary: Loop closure detection conventionally cascades separate models for global retrieval, geometric verification, and relative pose estimation, leading to redundant computation and disconnected visual representations. items.title: EEGDash Corpus: A Training-Ready Public Corpus for EEG Foundation Models
items.summary: Foundation models for electroencephalography (EEG) are pretrained on tens of thousands of hours of recordings, and their accuracy grows with that amount. Such data is hard to assemble. items.title: EnzymeRSI: A dual-loop recursive self-improvement system for enzyme design

items.summary: We investigate mixing dynamics in porous media at finite times, using pore-scale lattice-Boltzmann simulations combined with Lagrangian particle tracking. items.title: Annotator-Free Object Detection via Foundation Model Collaboration
items.summary: Object detection research remains constrained by high annotation costs and the closed-set assumptions of supervised models, limiting scalability to novel categories. items.title: XuanJian-DINOSAR: A SAR Foundation Model Based on Global and Local Semantic Consistency

items.title: Reglos: A Self-Evolving Personal Memory Agent with Recursive Self-Improvement
items.summary: Personal agents draw on past conversations to tailor their responses to each user. Such patches risk overfitting, because one tested only on the failures it targets can fix those cases and help nowhere else. We present Reglos, a training-free personal memory agent that tests whether harness changes help beyond the failures they were written to fix. items.title: Decouple to Reuse: Fine-Grained Knowledge Augmentation for Time Series Foundation Models

items.title: Gauge-invariant thermodynamic description of rotating black strings in 5D minimal supergravity via Kaluza-Klein reduction
items.summary: We develop a gauge-invariant formulation of the thermodynamics of rotating black strings in five-dimensional minimal supergravity through Kaluza-Klein reduction. The resulting four-dimensional theory is $\mathcal{N}=2$ supergravity coupled to a single vector multiplet, with prepotential $P=\frac{1}{3\sqrt{3}}\frac{X_1^3}{X_0}$. items.title: Ramified tori and Gelfand--Kirillov dimension of mod $p$ representations
items.summary: Let $K/\mathbb{Q}_p$ be a finite extension of degree $n$ with $p\geq3$, and let $D$ be the non-split quaternion algebra over $K$. We prove that every infinite-dimensional admissible smooth representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(K)$ or $D^\times$ with a central character and satisfying a Casimir annihilation condition has Gelfand--Kirillov dimension $n$. As a corollary, every infinite-dimensional admissible Banach representation whose locally analytic vectors have an infinitesimal character has dimension $n$, strengthening Sorgdrager's bound to an equality. items.title: Do Personal Adapters Carry Over Across Sessions? Separating Personal From Population Gains When Calibrating EEG Foundation Models for Motor Imagery
items.summary: arXiv:2609.34801v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Every new user of a motor imagery brain-computer interface must be calibrated, and users typically return on different days. A common approach with electroencephalography (EEG) foundation models fits a small personal adapter on a frozen backbone, but evaluations are usually confined to one session and rarely separate the user's own contribution from that of the population model. We quantified personal adapters with two paired contrasts, the net gain of a user's own adapter over the population model and its advantage over adapters fitted to other users, for three frozen foundation models (CBraMod, REVE and LaBraM). items.title: SpikeAD: Toward Multiplication-Free Spike-Controlled Neuromorphic Architecture for Energy-Efficient Small Object Detection
items.summary: arXiv:2611.00112v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Energy-constrained aerial platforms require accurate object detection under strict power and latency budgets, yet conventional inference remains bottlenecked by multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations. While spiking neural networks (SNNs) offer bio-inspired efficiency, many SNN detectors retain hybrid MACs in intermediate layers, or use spike-driven inference where multi-level spikes are interpreted as repeated binary events. We propose SpikeAD, a direct-trained spike-controlled neuromorphic aerial detector. In SpikeAD, sparse bounded integer spikes act strictly as multiplexer control signals for multiplier-free shift-add inference, preserving…

items.title: State-Dependent Memristor Dynamics for Device-Informed Spike-Timing-Dependent Plasticity in Spiking Neural Networks
items.summary: arXiv:2611.00119v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work investigates device-informed spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP) in spiking neural networks using a literature-derived threshold-memristor model. Local STDP commands determine programming polarity and a programming coordinate for state-dependent conductance updates in the first fully connected layer, while a backpropagation-trained readout performs classification. HSPICE simulations characterize thresholded, polarity- and state-dependent device dynamics and differential crossbar multiply-accumulate behavior. items.title: TTSonic: A Unified Framework for Composable and Controllable Speech Generation
items.summary: Modern text-to-speech (TTS) systems can synthesize natural and expressive speech, yet a practical speech foundation model must go beyond naturalness to offer stable quality, precise controllability, and a broad set of composable capabilities within a unified framework. We present TTSonic, a unified speech generation model that supports zero-shot TTS, voice cloning, prosody cloning, instruction following, voice conversion, and cloning from noisy reference speech. Rather than relying on separate task-specific models, TTSonic accommodates diverse conditioning signals, including text, natural language instructions, reference speech, and text-described timbre, within the same model framework.…

items.title: Biharmonic submanifolds in nonpositive space forms
items.summary: We prove that there are no proper biharmonic submanifolds with parallel normalized mean curvature vector field in a nonpositive space form, in arbitrary dimension and codimension. We also prove that every biharmonic surface with flat normal bundle in a four-dimensional nonpositive space form is minimal. These results provide substantial support for Chen's conjecture and the generalized Chen's conjecture for hyperbolic space in higher codimensions.

items.title: Responsible AI in Academic Research: A Systematic Review of Ethical Principles, Challenges, and Future Directions
items.summary: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is now present in every stage of the academic research life cycle, yet the rules governing its use remain fragmented. Following PRISMA 2020, this systematic review used 34 structured search strings and citation chasing to search literature published between 2015 and 2025. Of 359 records identified, 124 studies and documents met the inclusion criteria: 40 empirical studies, 43 conceptual analyses or commentaries, 20 policy and guidance documents, 17 reviews and 4 methodological frameworks; 83% were published from 2023 onwards. Guidance converges on a narrow set of standards: AI cannot be an author, material use must be disclosed, and humans remain…

items.title: LFM4Ads: Large Foundation Model for Ads Recommendation
items.summary: Recent work leverages large-scale pretrained foundation models (FMs) to transfer generalizable representations to downstream advertising tasks. Most existing paradigms transfer user representations (URs) and item representations (IRs), while underutilizing the user-item cross representations (CRs) generated by deeper interaction layers. Although a recent approach transfers target-aware embeddings (TAEs), it requires real-time upstream FM inference alongside downstream model inference, introducing additional engineering complexity and overhead. To address these limitations, we propose Large Foundation Model for Ads Recommendation (LFM4Ads), an efficient pretrain-then-transfer framework for…

items.title: ACF7 promotes spontaneous metastasis in HER2-driven breast cancer through cytoskeletal coordination
items.summary: Abstract Background: Metastasis is the primary cause of breast cancer mortality, yet the cellular mechanisms that confer metastatic competence remain incompletely understood. Directed migration requires coordinated regulation of the actin and microtubule cytoskeletons, but how this integration contributes to metastatic progression in vivo remains unclear. Here, we investigated the role of ACF7, a spectraplakin that links actin filaments and microtubules downstream of HER2 signaling, in spontaneous metastasis of HER2-driven breast cancer. Methods: We generated a genetically engineered mouse model combining HER2-driven mammary tumorigenesis with conditional loss of ACF7, enabling its…

items.title: Flexible Artificial Neurons Based on NbOx for Robust Tactile Perception in a Wide Temperature Range.
items.summary: Neuromorphic tactile sensing that emulates biological touch enables artificial systems to work with high efficiency and low energy consumption. As tactile-sensing scenarios may involve curved surfaces and different temperatures, artificial spiking afferent neurons require both flexibility and temperature robustness at the front end of artificial systems. Here, we report flexible artificial spiking neurons based on niobium oxide (NbOx) threshold-switching (TS) memristors prepared on polyimide (PI) substrates. Temperature-dependent transport analysis indicates that their temperature robustness is associated with a bulk switching pathway in the NbOx film. By integrating an oscillation…

items.title: A comprehensive review of biosignal foundation models
items.summary: Abstract Foundation models are emerging as a promising approach to biosignal analysis, offering solutions to common challenges in learning from biosignal data, such as high variability, noise or limited annotations. This survey provides a comprehensive review of the state-of-the-art in this rapidly advancing field. We introduce commonly used biosignal modalities (including EEG, ECG, EMG, EOG and PPG) and discuss their defining characteristics with respect to training large models. We present a structured survey of existing work across unimodal and multimodal settings covering data processing, feature extraction, model architectures, pre-training paradigms and evaluation methods. We…

items.title: The AI Is Only Human: Why a Superintelligence May Not Kill Us
items.summary: Would a machine that understands the world, and us, far better than we do have the right to decide what happens to us? This essay starts from a comparison Yuval Noah Harari made in an October 2026 interview: that we might come to stand to a superior intelligence roughly as cattle stand to us. We have occupied the farmer's side of that relation for about ten thousand years, and the view has not improved our manners. The argument it makes is small. Being better at working out consequences settles what follows from one's ends, not which ends to have. Calculative superiority alone therefore establishes no moral priority of a machine's ends over ours, and none of ours over a machine's. The…

items.summary: The El-Rakhawi Bio-Energetic Computing Framework (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23912465) pioneers sustainable AI by bridging the AI energy crisis with biological computation paradigms. items.title: Coacervate droplets as a liquefier for the solid-to-liquid transition of RNA aggregates
items.summary: Abstract Biomolecular condensates are functionally gated by their material properties. While RNA is a primary structural scaffold, its sequence-specific interactions can aberrantly drive condensates into dysfunctional solid aggregates. Yet, actively reversing this solidification to restore function remains a fundamental challenge, impeding progress in synthetic biology and therapeutics interventions. Here, we establish that complex coacervates can be engineered as liquefiers to actively remodel solid RNA-peptide aggregates into functional liquid droplets. items.title: Why do some fungi grow fast and others slowly? The fungal growth-rate hypothesis
items.summary: In general, there is a dichotomy in growth mode between ‘moulds’ (filamentous ascomycetes and mucoromycetes), and ‘mushrooms’ (filamentous basidiomycetes): mould mycelia tend to grow fast, to be short-lived and to produce asexual spores, while mushroom mycelia tend to grow slowly, are among the longest-lived organisms known and generally do not produce asexual spores. I propose that this dichotomy is due to a fundamental difference in growth strategy. On one hand, mould mycelia typically grow like a ‘pyramid-scheme’: an exponentially increasing number of hyphae provides the mycelium with a constant supply of a growth-limiting nutrient such as nitrogen. However, ‘the pyramid scheme crashes’…

items.title: Quality Characteristics of Plant-Based Patties Formulated with Lentinula edodes Mycelium Produced by Submerged Fermentation and Different Fat Levels
items.summary: Mushroom mycelium is gaining attention as a sustainable protein source because it can be produced reliably through submerged fermentation and has a low environmental impact. In this study, we investigated the physicochemical and sensory characteristics of plant-based (PB) patties formulated with Lentinula edodes mycelium (LM) and pork backfat at respective levels of 15/0, 10/5, 5/10, and 0/15% (w/w, wet basis), based on the total formulation weight, and compared them with pork patties. Proximate composition analysis showed that the PB patty treatments had lower fat content (0–10.68%) than the control (p 0.05). These results suggest the feasibility of developing low-fat plant-based patty…

items.title: When perfect is a warning: explanations expose shortcuts that accuracy hides in cancer gene-expression classifiers
items.summary: When the classes in a training set come from different data sources, a classifier can score near-perfectly while learning where a sample came from. We show this for cancer classifiers trained on tumours from The Cancer Genome Atlas and normal tissue from the Genotype-Tissue Expression project. Six model families, including a tabular foundation model, reached an area under the curve of 1.000 yet called 80–97% of tumour-adjacent normal tissue cancer, and 100% in an independent cohort; a few matched normal samples per tissue removed most of this shortcut. Near-perfect accuracy could not tell a shortcut from an honestly easy task, flagging 87–92% of models trained on such tasks. We introduce a…

items.title: Pathology foundation-model embeddings reveal a morphological landscape of breast lesions beyond diagnostic categories
items.summary: Background Despite rapid advances in computational pathology, including foundation-model embeddings, most approaches remain classifier-based. Breast lesion pathology is an area of unmet clinicopathological need and a compelling setting for morphology-based modeling: diagnostic categories occupy overlapping morphological spectra and reflect heterogeneous pathways of tumor development, thereby posing substantial challenges for pathological diagnosis and subsequent clinical decision-making. However, approaches to delineate morphological continua across diagnostic categories and tumor development remain understudied. Here, we leveraged morphology-based foundation-model embeddings to define a…

items.title: PhenoMe: An interactive AI framework for interpretable, microscopy-driven phenotyping
items.summary: Extracting meaningful biological patterns from microscopy image datasets requires tools that quantitatively connect visual similarities and experimental context. Deep learning models, and in particular novel foundation models, have the capacity to translate images into high-dimensional embeddings that can better represent complex visual patterns. Using these complex representations analytically and linking them to experimental information, it is possible to build advanced exploratory and phenotyping capabilities. Here, we present PhenoMe, an open-source, model-agnostic framework to handle pretrained foundation model-derived image representations alongside quantitative image properties and…

items.title: Transport of Compensated Baryon-Asymmetry Domains in an Expanding Universe with Exact Spherical Diffusion and a Conditional Scalar-Field Test
items.summary: Abstract This paper examines how diffusion changes a finite, globally compensated baryon-asymmetry profile in an expanding, spatially flat Friedmann-Lema\^{i}tre-Robertson-Walker universe. Coupled baryon and antibaryon balance equations are reduced to an equation for the signed asymmetry, and the conditions for conservation of its spatial integral are stated. Using the accumulated comoving diffusivity, we derive the exact three-dimensional heat-kernel response for a spherical positive core surrounded by an oppositely signed shell whose amplitude is fixed by volume compensation. items.title: Matter-Dilution-Triggered Recollapse and Conditional Nonsingular Cycles in a Metastable Dark-Energy Model
items.summary: Abstract Can the dilution of matter end the cosmological expansion and start a new hot phase? We study a scalar field coupled to dark matter through \(\:A\left(\varphi\:\right)=1+{\varphi\:}^{2}/2{M}^{2}\). The coupling holds a vacuum with the observed dark-energy density while the dark-matter density exceeds a critical value, and releases it into a negative vacuum once the expansion has diluted the matter. While the field is held, the homogeneous background reproduces the standard cosmological model to numerical accuracy; after the release the expansion turns around tens of billions of years later. items.title: Device Stochasticity Directly Implements Bayesian Sampling in Spiking Neurons.
items.summary: Device stochasticity is considered a non-ideality in neuromorphic hardware, although stochastic neural activity supports probabilistic computation in biological systems. We show that intrinsic stochastic switching of magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) can be mapped to stochastic-threshold spiking neurons, providing a physical sampling primitive for Bayesian spiking inference. We develop a spiking Bayesian neural network (SBNN) with neuronal threshold distributions learned during training and sampled during inference. items.title: Enhanced Nonlinear Capacity of a Trapped-Ion Quantum Memristor Reservoir
items.summary: Abstract We present a numerical study of a quantum memristor (QM) reservoir based on a trapped-ion platform. The reservoir exploits nonlinear input-output mapping arising from Born-rule nonlinearity, quantum coherences, and feedback-induced fading memory to process classical time-series data.We benchmarked the performance of the QM reservoir on monomial approximation, NARMA, Mackey-Glass, and the Santa Fe time series, standard tasks in reservoir computing and quantum reservoir computing (QRC). items.title: Learning inhibitor interactions from protein deep mutational scanning data and deep learning models
items.summary: Recent advances in protein language models, geometric deep learning, and structure prediction frameworks have the potential to accelerate computational drug discovery. However, it remains unclear how well these methods generalize beyond their training sets. Mutation-dependent drug responses present a challenge to these methods because there are often large effects from relatively small perturbations. Here, we systematically benchmark diverse mutational effect and drug-target affinity prediction models using deep mutational scanning datasets spanning 11 inhibitor conditions for the MET kinase domain. items.title: Evaluating Uncertainty Calibration in Probabilistic Time Series Foundation Models
items.summary: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) are increasingly used for probabilistic forecasting across diverse domains, yet the reliability of their uncertainty estimates remains poorly understood. In this work, we study uncertainty calibration in probabilistic TSFMs from a broader methodological and empirical perspective. We introduce a taxonomy of how TSFMs represent predictive uncertainty and develop a fine-grained evaluation framework for calibration in multi-horizon forecasting that distinguishes pooled, horizon-wise, and stronger conditional notions of calibration. items.title: I want to Break Free: The Positive Side of Symmetry Breaking
items.summary: We study the role of internal field-space symmetries in Effective Field Theories constrained by positivity bounds. For theories with $N$ real scalar fields, we classify derivative operators according to the internal symmetries they preserve, organising them into hierarchies based on the maximal symmetry $O(N)$ and its subgroups. We find that the Wilson coefficients of operators that depart from an enhanced symmetry are bounded in terms of those that respect it. items.title: DBI Softens Stiff-Phase Gravitational-Wave Spectra
items.summary: We investigate the effect of non-canonical kinetic terms on the present-day density spectrum of primordial gravitational waves (GWs), by considering the dynamics of a scalar field governed by the Dirac--Born--Infeld (DBI) action and a runaway potential. items.title: Symmetry breaking from conformality loss on holographic Rényi defects
items.summary: The Rényi entropies of a ball are computed by a conformal defect, the Rényi defect, dual in holography to a hyperbolic black hole. items.title: ASCoR: Asymmetric Semantic-Spatial Learning for Remote Sensing Domain Generalization
items.summary: Source-only domain generalization (DG) for remote sensing semantic segmentation seeks reliable predictions in unseen domains without target-domain data during training. Although vision foundation models offer transferable knowledge, category recognition remains sensitive to source-specific visual cues, while task-specific adaptation may weaken pretrained transferability. We propose ASCoR, an asymmetric semantic-spatial framework built on SAM3. Its text-conditioned semantic branch uses class-name prompts to provide explicit category guidance. items.summary: We develop detailed quaternionic and octonionic frameworks for quantum computation grounded on normed division algebras. Our central result is to prove the polynomial computational equivalence of quaternionic and complex quantum models: Computation over $\mathbb{H}$ is polynomially equivalent to the standard complex quantum circuit model and hence captures the same complexity class BQP up to polynomial reductions. items.title: Higher dimensional Kleinian groups of small Hausdorff dimension are classical Schottky groups II
items.summary: This is the higher dimensional continuation of our works on Hausdorff dimension of Kleinian groups \cite{Hou2010}, \cite{Hou2020}. In this paper we prove that for all $r\ge 2$ there exists $λ_r>0$, which is independent of the dimension $N$ of the hyperbolic space, such that any finitely generated non-elementary torsion-free Kleinian group of $\Isom(\mathbb{H}^N)$ generated by $r$ elements with limit set of Hausdorff dimension $<λ_r$ is a classical Schottky group. items.title: Supersymmetric Neuromorphic FitzHugh--Nagumo model
items.summary: We develop a supersymmetric spectral description of stochastic FitzHugh--Nagumo dynamics motivated by an effective antiferromagnetic neuromorphic model. items.title: Separatrix splitting in a multiferroic neuromorphic oscillator: toward Arnold diffusion
items.summary: Prototype magnetic neuromorphic systems, in essence, are based either on ferromagnetic or antiferromagnetic materials as key elements for conventional neuromorphic setups. In this work, we propose a novel neuromorphic system based on a ferromagnetic disk and a ferroelectric layer coupled via the magnetoelectric effect. We study a magnetoelectrically coupled ferromagnetic--ferroelectric oscillator as a candidate element for neuromorphic devices. items.title: A Common Language for Dynamic Graphs: Interaction Tokenization Enables Foundation Models
items.summary: Dynamic graphs capture evolving interactions in Web systems, including online communication, user engagement, and recommendation. Graph foundation models aim to reuse predictive capabilities across networks, but extending this capability to dynamic graphs faces two challenges. First, node identities are graph-specific, and similar interaction patterns can appear at different temporal and activity scales, making histories difficult to represent consistently across networks. Second, the predictive roles of historical patterns vary across interaction dynamics, limiting transfer from a narrow range of training processes. items.title: Axion 1.0: Open Agent Foundation Models, Simplified
items.summary: We introduce Axion 1.0, a fully open agent foundation model that combines strong and broad agentic capabilities with a remarkably simple training recipe. Axion 1.0 is trained in only three stages: two lightweight supervised fine-tuning stages followed by reinforcement learning, without dedicated mid-training, direct preference optimization (DPO), or on-policy distillation (OPD). The first SFT stage develops strong self-contained reasoning through model-aware data construction, where we synthesize challenging problems and adversarially strengthen them based on the base model's own successful solution strategies. items.title: Can Coding Agents Sustain Continual Evolution without Forgetting?
items.summary: Recently, harness self-evolution has emerged as an important paradigm for improving agent performance. Prior studies show that evolving the agent harness can effectively enhance agent capabilities without modifying the foundation model's parameters. Whether an agent harness can continuously evolve across multiple tasks without suffering from catastrophic forgetting remains an important open question. items.title: Neumann problem for Hessian equation and geometric inequalities in hyperbolic space
items.summary: We establish the existence of solutions to the Neumann problem for the Hessian equation on a smooth, bounded strictly static convex domain in hyperbolic space. The boundary condition determines a unique compatibility constant, and admissible solutions are unique up to a multiple of the static potential. As an application, we give a direct analytic proof of some weighted geometric inequalities for the static convex domain in hyperbolic space.

items.title: LaBraM at Scale: Scaling Data and Models for EEG Pretraining
items.summary: LaBraM, an early EEG foundation model, demonstrated that large-scale EEG pretraining can yield strong representations for diverse downstream tasks. items.summary: The spectral instability of black holes has become a central topic of the black-hole spectroscopy program. items.title: Can You Predict the Next Mind? Toward Multi-Turn Multi-Party Mental World Modeling
items.summary: While multimodal foundation models have achieved remarkable progress in physical world modeling, generation, and embodied reasoning, their capacity for dynamic mental world modeling remains underexplored. Existing benchmarks predominantly focus on static mental state perception or short-horizon decision-making, overlooking the dynamic mental trajectories inherent in multi-party, multi-turn interactions. To bridge this gap, we introduce M$^3$WME-Bench, a benchmark designed to evaluate mental world modeling conditioned on the evolving actions of interactants. items.title: Why Tabular Foundation Models Excel on Relational Data They Have Never Seen
items.summary: Given a relational database (RDB) storing heterogeneous tabular information, how can we predict missing (or future) values in some target column of interest? items.title: Periodic KPP equations in hyperbolic space
items.summary: We study Fisher-KPP equations on hyperbolic space with reactions periodic in a Busemann coordinate or in the distance from a point or a geodesic. items.title: Control Foundation Models across Changing Block Diagrams: Generalizing Time-Series Prediction to Dynamic Graphs
items.summary: In the prediction and control of physical systems, combining records from different experiments and operations is expected to supply information that no single experiment provides on its own. items.title: Zero-shot time-series foundation models against the Khepri v1.5 baselines for 96-hour carbon-intensity forecasts in nine Nordic bidding zones: a preregistered comparison

items.title: AnchorHEC: Targetless Hand-Eye Calibration of Wrist and Fixed Cameras
items.summary: Recent robot systems combine wrist and fixed cameras, requiring camera-to-robot transforms for both. Most hand-eye calibration methods rely on targets or robot-body observations. items.title: Solv3R: 3D Looped Transformer as a Multi-view Solver
items.summary: Classical structure-from-motion reconstruction proceeds iteratively, refining camera poses and scene geometry from a current estimate. This allows maps to easily expand without recomputing already computed views, or geometry estimates to improve as more observations are provided. Most geometric foundation models, however, predict entire geometry in a single forward pass or update a recurrent state as frames arrive sequentially, making this expansion and refinement non-trivial. We introduce Solv3R, a looped transformer that learns to continue solving multi-view geometry from its current state. items.title: CARE: Grounded Recursive Self-Improvement for Production Customer-Service Agents
items.summary: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) in production agents involves transforming accumulated experience into reliable model updates while adapting to evolving business policies. We present CARE (Customer-service Agent Retrospective and Evolve), a grounded RSI framework that operationalizes this process in customer service. Its goal is to replace a frontier proprietary incumbent with an in-house mid-sized model that continues learning after deployment. After a one-time cold start on governed production traces, the current model serves production traffic alongside the incumbent, and its own failures drive the next update. items.title: SynForecast: Controlled Synthetic Time Series for Forecasting Research
items.summary: Synthetic time series constitute a substantial share of the training corpora of several recent forecasting foundation models. Existing studies report benefits at small data budgets and modest synthetic proportions, but each evaluates individual combinations of model and generator. Studying these benefits systematically requires generators that support controlled configuration, perturbation, reproducibility and mechanism-level ablation, and the 11 existing generators we review show gaps in this combined support. items.title: Investigating the effects of the patch size in Time Series Foundation Models
items.summary: Patch size is a central design choice in patch-based time-series foundation models, controlling temporal resolution, sequence length, and computational cost. We study how this choice interacts with transformer architecture through a controlled comparison of encoder-only and decoder-only forecasting models trained with the same data mixture and optimization budget. Across 97 GIFT-Eval tasks, encoder-only models consistently benefit from smaller patches, whereas decoder-only performance follows a U-shaped trend, with an intermediate patch size performing best in aggregate. items.title: Beyond Answers, Traces, and Efficiency: Evidence for Adaptive Reasoning
items.summary: Current AI systems are evaluated as reasoners through final-answer accuracy, reasoning traces, process supervision, and computational or human-relative efficiency. Yet these measures do not establish whether reasoning adapts when tasks or evidence change. We distinguish across-task adaptivity, where acquired abstractions transfer or recombine across novel problems, fromwithin-task adaptivity, where hypotheses and actions are revised in response to new observations, feedback, or counterexamples. items.title: THE STORY OF VINCA ALKALOIDS: NATURE'S CONTRIBUTION TO ONCOLOGY
items.summary: Vinca alkaloids are important plant-derived compounds that have made a major contribution to modern cancer therapy. Vincristine and vinblastine were discovered from the Madagascar periwinkle (Catharanthus roseus) in the 1950s after researchers unexpectedly observed a reduction in white blood cells rather than the expected antidiabetic effect. These compounds work by interfering with microtubule formation, thereby stopping rapidly dividing cells and leading to cell death. Several bioactive molecules, including vinpocetine, vinflunine, and vinorelbine, are commercially available and are used as medicinal drugs for neurological disorders and various cancers. items.title: Governing artificial intelligence in Australian healthcare organisations - a qualitative study of staff perspectives.
items.summary: Objective This study aims to examine how healthcare staff conceptualise artificial intelligence (AI) governance and to develop an understanding of organisational requirements to support safe and responsible AI use within health services. Methods This qualitative study was conducted within a major Australian healthcare organisation delivering care across three hospital campuses and community-based services. Twenty-three semi-structured interviews were undertaken with staff and representatives across strategic leadership, clinical implementation, research and evaluation, governance and regulation, operational delivery, legal oversight, and consumer engagement.
